title: Pink ball in daytime Tests, penalties for time-wasting: ICC announces new playing conditions across menâs and womenâs cricket
text: England batsman Zak Crawley and India captain Shubman Gill exchange words after Crawley called for the doctor after being hit on the finger during day three of the Third Test Match at Lord's Cricket Ground on July 12, 2025 in London, England. (Photo/Getty Images) The International Cricket Council (ICC) on Thursday introduced several changes to the playing conditions in men's and women's cricket, including penalties for batters who waste time, tighter specifications for balls used in women's cricket, the option of pink balls in daytime Test matches and a rule change for the final over of a day's play. The changes will apply to all international series beginning on October 1 or later, while series that are already underway will continue under the existing regulations. Watch Sitanshu Kota on Shubman Gillâs 200 & Rohit Sharmaâs stunning start The updated Playing Conditions for men and women across all formats incorporate changes to the MCC Laws of Cricket that come into effect on Thursday. The changes have been introduced to "address time-wasting, standardise ball specifications and clarify certain aspects of fielding." Batters to face penalties for wasting time The playing condition for time-wasting by batters has been revised in men's cricket. If a batter is not ready to face the next delivery within the prescribed time, they will receive a warning for the first offence and a final warning for the second. A third offence, and every subsequent offence, will result in five penalty runs being awarded to the fielding team. Code of Conduct provisions may also be used if a batter repeatedly wastes time. New ball specifications for women's cricket The ICC has introduced tighter limits on the size and weight of balls used in women's international cricket. Men's cricket already has limited tolerances for ball size and weight. However, manufacturers have often produced one ball for both women's and junior cricket. The new rules introduce three separate size and weight specifications for men's, women's and junior cricket. A new men's ball must weigh between 5.5 and 5.75 ounces (156-163 grams) and measure 22.4-22.9 centimetres in circumference. For women's cricket, the ball must weigh 5-5.25 ounces (142-149 grams) and measure 21.5-22 centimetres in circumference. Overthrows clarified Following MCC recommendations, The ICC has also clarified what constitutes an overthrow. An overthrow is defined as an attempt to direct the ball towards the stumps to prevent runs or complete a run-out. A misfield, whether the fielder is trying to stop the ball or pass it to another fielder, will not be considered an overthrow. Greater flexibility over when a ball is finally settled Umpires will now have greater discretion in deciding when a ball is "finally settled", which can be particularly important on the final delivery of a close match. The ball no longer has to be in the bowler's or wicketkeeper's hands for it to be considered finally settled. Greater clarity on fielders holding the ball For a ball to be considered held by a fielder during a run-out or stumping, the fielder must have complete control of it. Simply touching the ball with a hand while it breaks the stumps will not be enough to establish that the ball was held. Changes specific to Test cricket Pink balls in daytime Tests: Pink balls may be used on a trial basis in daytime Test matches if both teams agree before the match. The change is aimed at reducing loss of playing time because of bad light. Once a Test begins with a pink ball, the decision cannot be changed and the pink ball must be used for the remainder of the match. A switch from a red ball to a pink ball after the start of the Test will not be allowed. The ICC said the change was made because stopping at the fall of a wicket does not save time, as the remaining deliveries still have to be bowled the following day. title: Abhishek Sharma's 30-ball ton hid the number that should really worry T20 bowlers
text: Abhishek Sharma The 30-ball ton was, oddly, the least surprising part of what Abhishek Sharma did at the Arun Jaitley Stadium. It isn't even his fastest hundred. What's odd about the innings is what it says about the number sitting next to that extraordinary strike rate: his average. Somewhere in Abhishek Sharma's memory, though, there's a faster century still. It came two years ago, for Punjab against Meghalaya in a Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy fixture nobody outside domestic cricket was watching: 28 balls, no fanfare. Watch Prasidh Krishna press conference: Virat Kohli, Gurnoor Brar and bowling depth So when he reached three figures in 30 deliveries against Afghanistan in New Delhi, becoming the fastest T20I centurion ever produced by a Full Member nation and only the third-fastest in the format's history overall, it wasn't a discovery. It was a confirmation, delivered on a bigger stage, of something the data had already been saying for a while. Abhishek Sharma scores in the India vs Afghanistan T2OI series The ground has some history with him already. Eight years earlier, on the same square when it was still called Feroz Shah Kotla, a 17-year-old Sharma walked out at number six for Delhi Daredevils against Royal Challengers Bangalore and top-scored on IPL debut â an unbeaten 46 off 19 balls. It was the innings that first put his name into circulation. None of that is really the story, though. The story is what his average has been doing while all this has been going on. The average, not the strike rate After 58 T20I innings, Abhishek averages 33.18 at a strike rate of 194.55. Among those who have batted at least 20 times in T20Is since Abhishek's debut in July 2024, nobody has struck as quickly as his 194.55 per 100 balls. Abhishek Sharma fast and consistent not fast or consistent Put that alongside the numbers of his closest opening peers and the combination starts to look strange. Phil Salt, across almost the same number of innings, averages 34.34 at 165.89: a fraction higher on average, nearly thirty runs per hundred balls slower. Finn Allen's numbers read 28.67 and 170.74; Travis Head's, 28.40 and 156.69. Multiply strike rate by average and divide by 100 and you get a rough figure for scoring speed without giving up the average: Abhishek comes out at 64.56, against 56.97 for Salt, 48.95 for Allen and 44.50 for Head. The gap isn't really about six-hitting or bravado. It's that T20 cricket generally punishes extreme aggression with a lower average, and in Abhishek's case, over more than fifty innings now, it hasn't. Where the runs actually come from Look closer and the shape of his batting explains some of it. Of his 1,858 T20I runs, 1,484 (79.9%) have come in boundaries. In the Afghanistan innings that figure spiked to 94.44%, the highest boundary share recorded in any men's T20I century. A six every 7.58 balls He hits a six in T20Is every 7.58 balls, comfortably ahead of Allen (8.47), Salt (12.47) and Head (14.20). Zoom out to his whole T20 career, across formats, and he reached his hundredth six faster, by balls faced, than anyone the format has seen, edging West Indies' Evin Lewis. Among Indian batters with 50 or more T20 sixes, nobody has matched his rate of clearing the boundary. He's the best of the lot, streets ahead of Sanju Samson, Shivam Dube, Suryakumar Yadav and Yuvraj Singh , the mentor whose fastest-fifty record he's now threatened on at least three occasions. Most sixes for India in a T2OI match The first six overs The clearest expression of the method is the powerplay. His strike rate in an innings' first ten balls, 176, is the joint-highest on record, level with Tim David: he isn't feeling out the pitch before he attacks. His boundary percentage inside the powerplay, 33.48% according to CricViz, is the best among batters with 500-plus T20I runs. Abhishek owns India's big Powerplays This has happened before, too. India have breached 90 in a T20I powerplay four times, and Abhishek has been the one doing the damage on every occasion: 59 not out off 21 against England at the Wankhede last year, 51 not out off 14 against New Zealand in Guwahati this year, 51 off 19 in the World Cup final in Ahmedabad, where he reached fifty in 18 balls under the most pressure he's likely ever faced. His 76 not out off 22 balls is simply the largest number yet on that list. His opening stand with Samson, 142 off 59 balls, is now the fastest century opening partnership for India in T20Is by run rate, overtaking a stand between KL Rahul and Rohit Sharma from Indore in 2017. What it costs him None of this comes free. Abhishek walked into this year's T20 World Cup and made three consecutive ducks, followed that with 15, 10 and 9, and salvaged the campaign with two match-defining fifties, one in a must-win Super Eight game against Zimbabwe, the other in the final. Eight innings, 141 runs, an average of 17.62. "As a batter, as a cricketer, sometimes [my form is] going to go up and down," he said afterwards, and there's little sense he sees the ducks as a separate problem from the sixes. They're the same bet, landing differently. What this approach costs Abhishek And 2026 has underlined that cost. Abhishek has been dismissed for a duck 10 times in T20 cricket this calendar year, the most by any batter in a year, ahead of Rashid Khan's nine in 2019 and Shadab Khan's nine in 2024. Five of those have come off the first ball, making him the joint-most prolific first-ball duck-maker in a calendar year in T20Is, alongside Rwanda's Kevin Irakoze in 2023 and Richard Ngarava in 2024. What's changed isn't the risk-taking. It's how deliberately he manages it. Against the Rashid Khan, Mohammad Nabi and Mujeeb Ur Rahman spin trio in the Afghanistan series, he made a conscious tactical switch, going only forward or down the pitch, never back, and scored 54 off 15 against them, including 4, 4, 6 off three straight Rashid deliveries in the last over of the powerplay. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines In the first two games, camped on the back foot against the same bowlers, he'd managed only 29 off 17. "It's always about me backing my shots because I don't have a lot of shots," he said earlier this year, after an 85 off 34 against New Zealand, which sounds like modesty until you notice how precisely that limited toolkit is being aimed. Level with Kohli Most T20 centuries by Indians This is now his tenth century in all forms of T20 cricket, level with Virat Kohli for the most by an Indian batter, and his third T20I hundred, level with Samson, and behind only Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav in India's own list. The number worth sitting with isn't the 30 balls. It's how Abhishek has managed to keep his average above 30 while scoring at a strike rate of nearly 195. title: ILT20 Season 5 Player Auction: Big names, purse remaining and everything you need to know
text: ILT20 Season 4 Player Auction (ILT20 Photo) The International League T20 (ILT20) Season 5 Player Auction will be held on Thursday, October 1, in Dubai, with more than 200 players from 23 countries set to go under the hammer. The auction pool features some of the biggest names in T20 cricket, including Babar Azam, Phil Salt, Tom Banton, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Wanindu Hasaranga, Alzarri Joseph, Faf du Plessis and Liam Livingstone. The six franchises will enter the auction with purses ranging from $1.3 million to $1.39 million, while they must build squads of between 18 and 23 players. Watch ILT20: Simon Helmot reveals Gulf Giantsâ strategy, key signings & auction Here is everything you need to know about the ILT20 Season 5 auction: Q. When and where is the ILT20 Season 5 auction? The auction will be held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at the ICC Academy Indoors in Dubai. Q. How many players are in the auction? More than 200 players from 23 countries have registered for the auction. The player pool includes cricketers from 11 ICC Full Member nations, as well as ILT20 partner nations Kuwait and Saudi Arabia and 10 other ICC Associate Member nations. Q. What are the player price categories? Players have been placed in three base-price categories: $80,000 $40,000 $10,000 The $80,000 bracket features several established T20 names, including Babar Azam, Phil Salt, Tom Banton, David Willey, Fakhar Zaman, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Jonny Bairstow, Moeen Ali, Liam Livingstone, Alzarri Joseph, Wanindu Hasaranga, Faf du Plessis, Alex Hales, Naseem Shah, Fazalhaq Farooqi and Chris Woakes. The $40,000 category includes Jayden Seales, Ibrahim Zadran, Shadab Khan, Tabraiz Shamsi, Avishka Fernando, Kusal Perera, Gulbadin Naib, Chris Green and Andre Fletcher. The $10,000 bracket features players such as Will Smeed, Lorcan Tucker, Reeza Hendricks, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Ish Sodhi, George Munsey, Matt Potts, Bas de Leede and Tanzim Hasan Sakib. Q. How the $10,000 category could be decisive in shaping the squads? The lowest base-price category could play an important role in squad building, particularly because franchises have significant roster requirements to fulfil. All players from UAE, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia will enter the auction at a base price of $10,000. ILT20 Season 4 Player Auction (ILT20 Photo) Q. Why are UAE players expected to attract attention? UAE, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia players could not be retained by franchises under the Season 5 recruitment rules. That means several established Gulf-region players will return to the auction pool, including UAE internationals Muhammad Waseem, Junaid Siddique, Haider Ali, Ayan Afzal Khan, Alishan Sharafu and Khuzaima Tanveer. Franchises will also have the option of using one Right to Match (RTM) on a UAE player who either represented them in Season 4 or played for them in the recently concluded ILT20 Development Tournament. Q. How much money does each franchise have to spend? Each team receives a base auction purse of $1.3 million, with any remaining money from the $700,000 allocated for pre-auction signings added to that purse. The available purses are: MI Emirates: $1.39m Abu Dhabi Knight Riders: $1.365m Desert Vipers: $1.305m Gulf Giants: $1.305m Dubai Capitals: $1.30m Sharjah Warriorz: $1.30m Q. What are the squad-size requirements? Every franchise must finish the auction with a minimum of 18 players and a maximum of 23 players. Each squad must contain: At least 11 players from ICC Full Member countries At least four Afghanistan players At least one Ireland player At least four UAE players At least one Kuwait player At least one Saudi Arabia player At least one additional ICC Associate player, excluding UAE, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia UAE players have entered the ILT20 Auction at a base price of $10,000. Q. How much must franchises spend? Each team must spend at least $1.5 million and no more than $2 million on its squad. After the auction, franchises can sign one Wildcard player for an additional maximum fee of $250,000. Q. What are the playing XI requirements? Every playing XI in Season 5 must include: At least two UAE players At least two Afghanistan players At least one additional Associate Member player The additional Associate slot can be filled by a third UAE player or a player from another Associate nation, including Kuwait or Saudi Arabia. Q. What happens if a player withdraws from the auction? All replacement players must have registered for the Season 5 auction. Any player who withdraws from the auction on or before October 1 will not be eligible to participate in Season 5 either as a replacement player or as a Wildcard signing. title: Virat Kohli will fall short of Sachin Tendulkarâs 100-century record: Former India cricketer makes big prediction
text: Virat Kohli and Sachin Tendulkar (AP Photo) Former India opener Aakash Chopra has predicted that Virat Kohli will finish his international career with 98 centuries. In a video posted by Cricinfo on X, Chopra was asked how many centuries Kohli would have by the time he retires. He replied 98. Kohli, who only plays ODI now, currently has 86 international centuries and needs 15 more to surpass Sachin Tendulkarâs record of 100 international hundreds. Watch Ishan Kishan press conference: On batting approach, tricky pitch & playing for a gold medal Tendulkar played 664 international matches across formats between 1989 and 2013. He scored 100 centuries, including 51 in 200 Tests and 49 in 463 ODIs. Arshdeep is Indiaâs leading wicket-taker in T20Is, with 140 wickets from 94 matches. However, he has played only 18 ODIs since making his debut against New Zealand in November 2022. title: Rajasthan Royals star creates history, surpasses Chris Gayle for highest T20 score
text: Rajasthan Royals' Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Dhruv Jurel (Reuters) Lhuan-dre Pretorius produced a record-breaking innings on Friday, smashing an unbeaten 188 off just 79 balls for South Africaâs Titans against the Knights in a CSA T20 Challenge fixture. The 20-year-old left-hander struck 15 fours and 13 sixes as he surpassed the previous highest individual score in T20 cricket, the 175 not out hit by former West Indies star Chris Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore against Pune Warriors India in the 2013 IPL . Watch Sanju Samson press conference: On Asian Games, Virat Kohli hundred and more Pretoriusâ breathtaking knock came at a strike rate of 237.97 and powered the Titans to 267 for three from their 20 overs. Pretorius appeared on course to become the first batter to score 200 in a T20 innings, but ran out of deliveries before reaching the landmark. His 188 not out now stands as the highest individual score in the 20-over format, ahead of Gayleâs 175 not out, while Aaron Finch âs 172 for Australia against Zimbabwe in 2018 remains the highest score in menâs T20 internationals. Pretoriusâ innings also capped a strong run of form. His previous appearance came for South Africa, when he smashed a 53-ball 101 against Namibia in a T20 international last month. Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines The young batter has, however, had to contend with injury setbacks during his recent rise. Highest individual scores in T20 cricket Lhuan-dre Pretorius â 188* (Titans vs Knights, October 3, 2026) Chris Gayle â 175* (Royal Challengers Bangalore vs Pune Warriors India, April 23, 2013) Aaron Finch â 172 (Australia vs Zimbabwe, July 3, 2018) Hamza Khan â 164* (Rwanda vs Ivory Coast, May 24, 2026) Pretoriusâ 188* has now rewritten the record books for the highest individual score in T20 cricket. Pretorius is also part of the Rajasthan Royals squad in the IPL, although opportunities have been limited so far. With the franchise having established left-handed opening options in Yashasvi Jaiswal and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 20-year-old has found it difficult to secure a regular place in the playing XI. His record-breaking knock for the Titans, however, is another reminder of his potential and could put him in the spotlight ahead of the next IPL season. title: India script history, become first team to register 200 T20I wins after edging Japan in thriller
text: India beat Japan by 2 runs. (Pic credit: BCCI) NEW DELHI: India scripted another milestone in their T20I history on Tuesday, becoming the first team to register 200 wins in men's T20 internationals, including victories achieved through Super Overs. The landmark 200th win came in dramatic fashion as the world champions survived a major scare from hosts Japan, edging them by just two runs in a rain-shortened one-off T20I at Sano. Watch Washington Sundar: India eye Asian Games gold after Japan preparations With the match reduced to five overs per side because of rain, India posted only 32/4 after opting to bat. Japan came agonisingly close in the chase, finishing on 30/3 as India held their nerve to complete a historic victory. India's journey to 200 T20I wins began with their inaugural victory against South Africa in Johannesburg in 2006. They reached 50 wins against Sri Lanka in Colombo in 2017, completed 100 victories against West Indies in Kolkata in 2022 and reached 150 against Australia in Gros Islet in 2024. The latest victory against Japan took them into uncharted territory. India reach 200 wins faster than ever India have now registered 200 wins from 291 T20Is, comfortably ahead of Pakistan, who have 174 wins from 299 matches. New Zealand are third with 137 wins from 267 matches, followed by South Africa with 131 from 235 and England with 130 from 233. India's progress through the 50-win milestones has also become increasingly rapid. They needed 83 matches for their first 50 wins, before taking 72 matches to move from 50 to 100. The next 50 came in 70 matches, while India required only 66 matches to move from 150 to 200 wins. The 200th victory, however, was far from routine. Axar, Washington help India survive Japan scare The low-scoring contest was dominated by spin, with the damp surface and slow outfield making stroke-making difficult. Japan's spinners troubled India's star-studded batting line-up from the beginning. Charlie Hara Hinze dismissed Abhishek Sharma for a duck, while Ibrahim Takahashi accounted for Sanju Samson, who made 10. Benjamin Ito-Davis then removed Ishan Kishan for three. Skipper Shreyas Iyer top-scored with 16, but India could manage only 32/4 from their five overs, hitting just three boundaries. Japan looked capable of producing one of the biggest upsets in their cricketing history during the chase. Ravi Bishnoi conceded 10 runs in the third over, while Washington Sundar's penultimate over went for seven as Japan moved within striking distance. Washington finished with 2/13, while Axar Patel's experience proved crucial in the final over. Rain had also left the outfield sluggish, making boundary-hitting even harder. There was late drama when a wide call against India in the final over was overturned after an appeal from Shreyas Iyer. Japan eventually finished on 30/3, falling two runs short. The result gave India their 200th T20I win in their historic first T20I against Japan, adding another landmark to the country's growing record in the format. title: 'No obligations under Rome Statute for overflights': France defends not arresting Netanyahu
text: Benjamin Netanyahu (File photo) France has defended its decision not to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu despite an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant against him. Netanyahuâs plane crossed French airspace on Thursday en route to the United Nations. As a signatory to the ICCâs founding Rome Statute, France is formally bound to cooperate with the court, including by arresting suspects who enter its territory. French foreign ministry spokesperson Pascal Confavreux told reporters the clearance to Netanyahu's aircraft was "in full conformity with international law." "The Rome Statute does not impose any obligations regarding overflights of its territory by a state plane which has a passenger who is targeted by an arrest warrant," Confavreux said. According to flight-tracking app Flightradar24, Netanyahuâs plane flew over Greece, Italy and France. An Italian foreign ministry spokesperson said they could not immediately confirm whether Israel had sought permission for the overflight. Netanyahu faces restrictions on travel to several countries because of an ICC arrest warrant issued against him and his former defence minister Yoav Gallant, as well as a separate warrant for a former Hamas military commander, in 2024. Last year, Netanyahu took a circuitous route to New York to avoid the airspace of several European countries, including France, according to media reports. Israel rejects the ICCâs jurisdiction and denies committing war crimes in Gaza. It says its military campaign was aimed at eliminating Hamas following the groupâs October 7, 2023, attack on Israel. Israel is contesting the warrants against Netanyahu and Gallant. The United States, a close Israeli ally and non-signatory to the Rome Statute, has launched a campaign to isolate the court. President Donald Trump this week urged members of The Hague-based court to leave what he called an âout of control institutionâ. France has condemned threats against the ICC. Netanyahu was making a brief visit to the US to address world leaders at the UN General Assembly and was expected to return to Israel later on Thursday. (With Reuters inputs) You use AI every day. title: After Madras HC rap, Puducherry govt suspends SP-rank officer
text: Madras high court PUDUCHERRY: Ticked off by Madras high court for its apparent reluctance to act, the Puducherry territorial administration on Friday suspended superintendent of police (SP) A Subramanian following allegations of sexual harassment made by a woman police officer in Karaikal. A division bench of high court expressed strong indignation at the procedural delays and the govt's apparent reluctance to act though a complaint had been filed by the woman police officerâs mother, alleging inaction by the Puducherry administration despite an internal inquiry confirming the charges. The bench urged the Puducherry administration to "wake up from its Kumbhakarna slumber" and play the role of Lord Rama as it claims to do. The bench warned that if action was not taken by Monday, the Puducherry chief secretary would be summoned to appear in person with all relevant files. According to the petition, Subramanian abused his official position to sexually harass the police constable stationed at Karaikal in 2024, during his tenure as Karaikal district SP. Distressed by the continuous harassment, the victim reportedly attempted suicide by consuming poison. The bench pointed out that the law mandated action within 60 days of an ICC report, noting that the deadline had long elapsed without any concrete measures being implemented. Although the internal complaints committee (ICC) submitted a report confirming the allegations of sexual harassment, no formal action was taken by the Puducherry govt, prompting the victim's family to approach the high court seeking justice. The bench said the files were merely moving from one desk to another, giving the impression of an attempt to protect the accused officer. Expressing deep distress, the bench remarked that it was painful to see the mother of a sexual harassment victim coming to court and crying for justice. Following the courtâs reprimand and ultimatum, the Puducherry chief secretary initiated departmental action, issuing an order suspending Subramanian from service based on the ICC report. The court has adjourned the next hearing to Monday. title: India survive Japan scare, defend lowest five-over T20 total by two runs
text: India survive Japan scare in five-over contest A bizarre wide call, an intervention from the square-leg umpire and a two-run escape. Indiaâs rain-shortened T20I against Japan had all the ingredients of a far more dramatic contest than a five-over game had any right to produce. With Japan needing eight runs in the final over, Alexander Shirai-Patmore attempted a reverse hit against Axar Patel off the overâs third ball. He was beaten. Japanese umpire Chris Thurgate called it a wide. Watch Washington Sundar: India eye Asian Games gold after Japan preparations The next ball produced an identical attempt and, again, wide was signalled. Wide-ball drama Suddenly, Japan needed only five from four balls. Indiaâs players were visibly unhappy. Then New Zealandâs Chris Brown , the square-leg umpire and a member of the ICC Elite Panel, intervened. After speaking to Thurgate, the decision was overturned and Japanâs equation was restored to six from four. It was the right call. Under the ICCâs guidelines, once a batter attempts a reverse or switch hit, both sides of the wicket are deemed off side for the purpose of judging wides. India still had to survive the over. Axar did, conceding only seven runs, and Japan finished on 30-3, two short of Indiaâs modest 32-4. After two days of heavy rain and a long wait for the ground to become playable in Sano, Japan, India ended up owning an enviable record â the lowest total successfully defended in a five-over T20 â and Japan wondering just how close they had come to one of the biggest upsets in their cricketing history. The conditions had made a mockery of conventional T20 logic. The surface was sticky and slow. The outfield was sluggish. All 10 overs were bowled by a spinner. There were just four boundaries across the entire game. India, asked to bat first, discovered the difficulty immediately. Abhishek Sharma was out first ball attempting a shovel sweep. The rest of Indiaâs top order struggled. Iyer alone managed a double-digit score, making 16 off 12. Hara-Hinze makes his mark Japanâs bowlers had done their job. Charlie Hara-Hinze, the 17-year-old left-arm spinner, took 2-17, while the entire attack exploited a surface on which timing the ball cleanly seemed almost impossible. Japanâs chase began badly. Axar conceded only two in his opening over, and Ishanâs direct hit from deep square leg accounted for Lachlan Yamamoto-Lake. title: 'The night I could not sleep': Gautam Gambhir opens up on 'toughest decision' to drop Sanju Samson for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
text: vaibhav sooryavanshi, gautam gambhir, sanju samson India head coach Gautam Gambhir has revealed the emotional difficulty behind one of his biggest selection calls in T20Is, admitting that dropping Sanju Samson during the England series left him unable to sleep. Samson, who was named Player of the Tournament during India's T20 World Cup triumph earlier this year, was left out after the first match of the five-game series in England in July. India had lost that opening T20I, with teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi coming into the XI for his T20I debut in Manchester. Watch Gautam Gambhir press conference: Samson vs Sooryavanshi and ODI World Cup plans Gambhir said the decision weighed heavily on him, particularly because Samson had played such an important role in India's World Cup success. Speaking to JioStar ahead of India's home season against the West Indies, the India coach revealed just how difficult the call was. "In two years of my journey, that was the only night I could not sleep and I told this to Sanju because I knew that it was probably the toughest decision in my coaching tenure in a T20 format because someone who was player of the tournament, and then you have to leave him out after three or four games. And the reason was probably Vaibhav was in that kind of form as well, and we had to win the series. âBecause ultimately you are there and when you are playing for India, or when you are coaching India, you want to win each and every series possible. I had a very, very honest conversation with him and I told him that that is one of the reasons why, because Vaibhav was in that kind of form, and we needed someone to score runs at the top, we needed that little bit of a platform at the top as well. And he was fine with it. And that's a conversation which me and Sanju had, and he took it in good spirits," said Gambhir. The call was eventually reversed when India returned home for their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan. Samson came back into the side at Sooryavanshi's expense and went on to hit back-to-back fifties as India completed a 3-0 series sweep. Gambhir also used the episode to explain why even a player in exceptional form cannot automatically expect a place in India's playing XI. "I know, it is (tough). But then, I made him understand that I know you're in good form, but sometimes with the players who have done well for a long time, you will have to wait for your opportunity. âThereâs one more thing - social media or outside noise doesn't decide the playing eleven. Playing eleven who, in that dressing room, or who the coach and captain feel can win us the match, or what is the best playing eleven, and who have done well for such a long time because if Vaibhav plays today, then it's going to be a tough conversation between me and whoever we leave out, whether it's Abhishek or Sanju. âSo we can't suddenly ignore that a combination that has created such an impact over the last one and a half or two years, that after three or four failures we drop them and play a young player who is very talented, who is also in very good form. âSo sometimes you will have to wait for your opportunity and we still want to create that security in that dressing room. Because it is very easy for me to take popular decisions, but it is probably the toughest thing for me to take the right decisions and we've taken the right decision of continuing with Sanju and Abhishek," he explained. Sooryavanshi's emergence has nevertheless added another dimension to India's T20I selection puzzle. The teenager made his international debut in Manchester, but Gambhir stressed that India's established combination cannot be discarded simply because a young player is performing well. title: US prepares sweeping sanctions on International Criminal Court
text: The International Criminal Court building is seen in The Hague, Netherlands (File photo) The Trump administration is preparing sweeping sanctions against the International Criminal Court that could restrict most of the Hague-based tribunal's financial transactions and potentially cut it off from much of the global banking system, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing US officials and documents. The measures would take effect after a six- to seven-month grace period and could prevent the court from conducting transactions in US dollars, according to the report. Transactions involving communications services would be exempt. Meanwhile, a State Department spokesperson pointed to Ssecretary of stateMarco Rubio's view that the ICC threatens US sovereignty. The administration could finalise the measures as early as this week, during the UN General Assembly in New York, or in the days that follow, according to the Journal. The proposed sanctions would go beyond existing US measures, which have targeted individual ICC officials including former chief prosecutor Karim Khan, ICC President Tomoko Akane, judges, deputy prosecutors and the prosecutor who led the case against Israeli officials. Washington's confrontation with the court intensified after the ICC issued arrest warrants in 2024 for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity linked to the Gaza war. Both have rejected the allegations. Rubio said in July that the administration would pursue a broad campaign against the court and would dismantle it "brick by brick" if necessary. He has argued that the ICC overstepped its authority by pursuing officials from countries that are not members of the court, including the United States and Israel. The US and Israel are not members of the ICC. The administration's position has drawn attention to Rubio's earlier stance on the court. As a US senator in 2022, he co-sponsored a resolution supporting an ICC investigation into alleged war crimes in Ukraine committed by Russia, another non-member state. The ICC later issued an arrest warrant for Russian President Vladimir Putin. European countries and other major ICC supporters, including Japan, have pledged to defend the court against US pressure, although it remains unclear what measures they could take to shield its operations from the proposed sanctions. title: Operation Sheruwali: How security forces tracked LeT commander Musa in months-long hunt since May
text: Hashim Moosa (Left) killed in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmirâs Budgam district, Indian Army (File photo) NEW DELHI: The killing of senior Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Musa in Jammu and Kashmir's Budgam district on Wednesday was the culmination of a months-long intelligence-led operation, named âOperation Sheruwaliâ, launched in May 2026. Security forces had been tracking Musa for a prolonged period before a coordinated plan involving multiple agencies was drawn up to neutralise him, following the receipt of technical and human intelligence about his movements and presence in the area. The operation culminated in an encounter in the Yousmarg area of Budgam, where Musa was killed. His body was later recovered along with war-like stores, according to the Army. Also read| Ex-Pakistan SSG commando, highly trained LeT terrorist, Pahalgam mastermind: Who was Hashim Moosa; killed in J&K encounter The ministry of information and broadcasting said the operation dealt a blow to the LeT network in Jammu and Kashmir, with Musa's killing bringing an end to a group of four senior commanders who had been operating in the union territory since 2022 and were linked to several attacks. Watch Operation Sheruwali Intensifies In Rajouri As Army Tightens Cordon Around Suspected Militants How Operation Sheruwali unfolded According to a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), security forces had been pursuing Musa for a long time. A specific plan involving all stakeholders was recently put in place after intelligence inputs indicated his movement and presence. The government said the operation to neutralise Musa was part of the ongoing âOperation Sheruwaliâ, which began in May 2026. The Army's Chinar Corps, meanwhile, said the encounter took place during Operation Korag in the Yousmarg area of Budgam district. Troops launched a search operation based on specific intelligence inputs and challenged suspicious movement, following which terrorists opened fire. The operation involved the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). The search continued after the encounter, with security personnel checking the surrounding areas for any additional terrorist presence. Musa's body was recovered from the general area of Palmaidan along with war-like stores, according to the Chinar Corps. Is Hashim Moosa an ex-Pakistan SSG commando? One of the key aspects of Musa's background is his alleged association with Pakistan's military. ANI, quoting security agency sources, reported that Musa had served as a para-commando in Pakistan's Special Service Group (SSG), where he held the rank of Havildar. According to the sources, he retired from the SSG in 2023, subsequently joined the LeT and infiltrated into India. Former Jammu and Kashmir DGP S P Vaid described Musa as a highly trained commando specialising in ambushes and guerrilla-style attacks. Vaid alleged that Musa's footprints had been seen in several attacks in Jammu and Kashmir, including those in Poonch, DKG, Bhimber Gali, Gulmarg and the attack on pilgrims in Reasi. However, his alleged military background has been reported by security agency sources and has not been independently established. Four-member LeT group neutralised With Musa's killing, all four senior LeT commanders belonging to the group that had been active in Jammu and Kashmir since 2022 have been neutralised, according to the government. The three other commanders were killed in separate encounters: Junaid Bhat: Neutralised on December 3, 2024, in Dachigam. Suleman: Killed on July 28, 2025, during Operation Mahadev. Yasir: Neutralised on September 4, 2026, during Operation Asdhar. The government linked the group to several attacks across Jammu and Kashmir, including the Halan attack in August 2023, DKG attack in December 2023, Kandi attack in May 2023, Shahsitar attack in May 2024, Shiv Khori attack in June 2024, Gagangir and Bootapathri attacks in October 2024, and the Baisaran attack in April 2025. Musa's alleged role in Pahalgam attack Musa was among the key suspects in the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack , in which terrorists targeted tourists at Baisaran Valley, killing 26 people. The Jammu and Kashmir Police had announced a reward of Rs 20 lakh for information leading to the arrest of Pakistan nationals and LeT terrorists Adil Hussain Thoker, Ali Bhai and Hashim Musa. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) subsequently chargesheeted seven accused in the case, including Pakistan-based LeT and The Resistance Front (TRF), which it accused of planning, facilitating and executing the attack. title: India survive huge Japan scare, win by two runs in historic T20I
text: India's Sanju Samson, left, bats against Japan (AP/PTI) India survived a massive scare against Japan to clinch a thrilling two-run victory in the historic one-off T20 International in Sano on Tuesday, with the run-truncated contest producing one of the closest finishes in the team's T20I history. After being reduced to just 32 for four in their five overs, India had their backs against the wall. But their spinners turned the contest around as Japan were restricted to 30 for nine in their five overs, allowing India to escape with a narrow victory. Watch Washington Sundar: India eye Asian Games gold after Japan preparations The result also saw India become the first team to register 200 wins in men's T20Is, including victories in Super Overs. India stunned by Japan's spinners The game had promised fireworks from India's batting line-up, but it was Japan's spinners who stole the show. With the match reduced to five overs per side after a delayed start caused by the wet outfield, Japan used spin for all five overs and found plenty of assistance from the surface. The ball began turning from the very first delivery and India's batters struggled to adapt. Abhishek Sharma was dismissed for a golden duck, while Sanju Samson followed in the next over. Ishan Kishan also failed to stay for long. Shreyas Iyer provided India's only substantial contribution with a 16-run knock, but India could manage only 32 runs from their five overs. The damp conditions made matters even harder for the batters. The outfield was slow and boundaries were difficult to come by, adding to the challenge of scoring quickly. Japan walked off after the innings with plenty to celebrate, having reduced one of the world's strongest T20I teams to such a modest total. India's spinners turn the game around Japan needed only 33 runs from five overs and appeared to have a huge opportunity to complete one of the biggest upsets in their cricketing history. But India's spin attack had other plans. Axar Patel, Washington Sundar and Ravi Bishnoi kept the pressure on Japan, exploiting the same conditions that had troubled India's batters. Japan struggled to build momentum and, despite needing just over six runs an over, could not get over the line. India eventually held their nerve to defend the tiny target and win by two runs. title: NMC Seeks Rs748.62Cr Grant From State To Compensate For Entertainment Tax Waiver
text: Ai image Nagpur: Cash-starved Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) has once again initiated efforts to secure a Rs748.62 crore grant from the state govt to compensate for the revenue lost due to suspension of entertainment tax collection. The tax was suspended after GST implementation in 2017. Around three years ago, the then municipal commissioner Abhijeet Chaudhari had written letters to the govt seeking the grant. However, no concrete assurance was received. NMC has started the process for sending a fresh proposal to the govt as temporary exemption from entertainment tax collection ended on Sept 30. Before GST came into force, a special department under the district collectorâs office collected entertainment tax. On May 29, 2017, the state govt amended the Maharashtra Entertainment Duty Act and transferred the power to collect the tax to local bodies. Subsequently, NMC started collecting entertainment tax from single-screen cinemas, multiplexes, cable connection operators and programmes organised at auditoriums and cultural halls, including ticketed social and cultural events. With implementation of GST from July 1, 2017, the state granted a temporary exemption from entertainment tax under Section 3 of the Maharashtra Entertainment Duty Act. The suspension resulted in a substantial loss of revenue for the civic body. The exemption, introduced in 2017, was extended by the state cabinet on May 3, 2023, under then chief minister Eknath Shinde , up to Sept 30, 2026. Before NMC, the district collectorate earned Rs20.24 crore from entertainment tax in 2015-16 and Rs24.01 crore in 2016-17. Had the collection continued, the annual revenue was projected to rise steadily over the years. As per the civic administrationâs estimates, the potential annual revenue loss has risen to Rs148.80 crore in 2026-27. âEntertainment tax was a major source of revenue for NMC. The grant, if provided, would bring financial relief for the civic body and help overcome fund constraints for development works,â said Milind Meshram, officiating additional municipal commissioner. Many of them travelled together from Tokyo, around 400 km by road, to Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan, turning the trip into an occasion of camaraderie, excitement and, of course, plenty of cricket moments. For club members, seeing one of sportâs most anticipated encounters from the stands was an opportunity they did not want to miss. âPreparations started at least five to six months ago when we bought the tickets online, expecting India to play in the finals. Pakistan being in the finals was the cherry on the cake,â said Choudhury Santoshi Prasad Mohanty, founder and vice-president of the club. Many Odias reached Nagoya, 30 minutes away from Nisshin, the night before the match and returned the day after. Most had worn Indian jerseys and carried Tricolour, placards and even cymbals to cheer the Indian team. A few had painted their hair and cheeks with Indian colours. They, however, had to wait outside the stadium for a considerable time for the bronze medal match between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh to get over. Out of the eight stands, Indian fans occupied at least six. Living in Japan, they get to watch fewer cricket matches, and watching a match of this scale is nearly impossible. âThough my home in Cuttack is close to Barabati Stadium and I often go there to play, getting to see traditional rivals India and Pakistan was a dream come true,â said Afroz Khan, a board member of the club. Most felt that they would never get to see a repeat of this match. The high-scoring match was thrilling, with each team matching the other till the last over. Every ball excited the audience. âIn Japan, people are very disciplined. None would stand up in the front rows so that the back benchers get a view,â said Khan. Of all the match scenes, the most cherished moment was when the Indian flag was hoisted and the national anthem was played after India received the gold medal from International Cricket Council chairman Jay Shah on winning the final against Pakistan. title: Two get 20 years in jail for raping minor who later gave birth
text: Jail term Ahmedabad: A special Pocso court in Ahmedabad on Monday sentenced two youths to 20 yearsâ imprisonment after holding them guilty of raping a minor girl, who later delivered a child at a young age. The convicts, both 22 years of age, were accused of establishing sexual relationships with the 16-year-old girl in 2024. While the first accused was in a relationship with the minor between Jan and May 2024, the second accused and the girl were together from May to Nov 2024, when the girl was found 28 weeks pregnant. When the family found out about her pregnancy, they lodged an FIR with Shahpur police. The childâs DNA samples established the first accused as the biological father, but the court found enough evidence against the second accused as well to convict him. Additional public prosecutor K G Jain examined 17 witnesses and presented 48 pieces of documentary evidence to establish guilt of both the accused. The court, after finding it a consensual relationship, awarded the minimum sentence of 20 years. The court also ordered Rs 10.5 lakh compensation for the victim for having undergone the trouble of becoming a mother at a very young age. title: Simi Singh: An Ireland dream, a life-threatening detour and the journey home
text: Simi Singh. (Photo by Donall Farmer/PA Images via Getty Images) NEW DELHI: Simranjit Singh, known as Simi Singh in Ireland and across world cricket, had already retired in his mind when acute liver failure brought his career to a shuddering halt in 2024. But on Wednesday, he closed the chapter officially, announcing his retirement and bringing down the curtain on a remarkable 20-year association with Ireland, the country he moved to in 2006 to pursue hotel management, only to find a second life in cricket. Over his two decades in Ireland, the highs were incredibly high, but the lows were devastating as well. Watch Ishan Kishan press conference: On batting approach, tricky pitch & playing for a gold medal âI played international cricket, represented Ireland in the World Cup (T20), scored a century while batting at No. 8 against South Africa in ODIs and picked up a five-wicket haul as well. Recently, I came to know that I have the best economy rate in ODIs (3.99), with Rashid Khan second. When I packed my bags and left for Ireland as a teenager, playing cricket was not something I had in my mind. It was special,â Simi told TimesofIndia.com. âThe people at Cricket Ireland were not surprised because, even before this, I was not being considered for selection. It had become difficult to play professional cricket, especially with my recovery still going on. So I thought it was better to properly close things and make an official announcement so that everyone knew,â added Simi, who played 35 ODIs and 53 T20Is for Ireland. In early 2024, Simiâs life was turned upside down after he developed a mysterious fever. Doctors in Ireland were unable to find the underlying cause and his health began to deteriorate. He eventually moved to India in search of better medical opinions, only to discover that he had developed acute liver failure. His wife, Agamdeep Kaur, donated part of her liver to save his life. âMy wife is my guardian angel. She was God-sent. She gave me a new life. It was a torrid time for the family,â he said. âNow I have moved back to Mohali. Recovery is still going on. There is improvement, but it is slow. I will survive,â he added. It was never all hunky-dory for Simi in Ireland. With tough residency rules, his ECB Level 2 coaching qualification and certification as a personal trainer helped him stay afloat before he eventually broke into the national team. Now, the coaching qualification he earned all those years ago has come to the fore. He has opened his own cricket academy in Mohali, the city where he toiled during his formative years and represented Punjab successfully at the U-14 and U-17 levels. âFor now, I am not running the academy myself. I have completed Level 2 with the England Cricket Board, and I am thinking of doing Level 3. Then we will see what opportunities come up,â he said. title: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 cr of 12.10 cr
text: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 crore NEW DELHI: The Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party received Rs 12.10 crore in contributions in 2025-26, a 68% drop from the previous financial year, according to its latest report filed with the Election Commission. Nearly 83% of the party's contributions came from two donors, Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited. Both gave Rs 5 crore each. Trident was founded by former AAP Rajya Sabha member Rajinder Gupta. The remaining contributions amounted to around Rs 2.10 crore, according to the report. Gupta was elected to the Rajya Sabha on an AAP ticket in October 2025. Trident's Rs 5-crore cheque was dated January 9, 2026, when Gupta was still with the AAP. He joined the BJP after Raghav Chadha led rebellion, merging two-third of AAP's Rajya Sabha strength into the ruling saffron party in April this year. The AAP had reported contributions of Rs 38.10 crore in 2024-25, compared with Rs 11.06 crore in 2023-24. Prudent Electoral Trust was the party's biggest donor that year, contributing Rs 16.40 crore. The latest filing covers the first full financial year after the AAP lost power in Delhi in February 2025. The party continues to govern Punjab, where Trident is based. The AAP report has 1,202 numbered entries. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora is listed against 12 payments of Rs 10,000 each, adding up to Rs 1.20 lakh. How other regional parties fared The latest filings of other regional parties also show a decline in contributions compared with 2024-25. The Telugu Desam Party (TDP), which came to power in Andhra Pradesh, reported Rs 58.25 crore in contributions in 2025-26, down from Rs 83.03 crore the previous year. Prudent Electoral Trust was its biggest donor, giving Rs 45 crore, compared with Rs 40 crore in 2024-25. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which lost power in Andhra Pradesh to the TDP, reported contributions of Rs 24.31 crore. This was sharply lower than the Rs 140.04 crore it reported in 2024-25. Its biggest donor in the latest filing was Goodwood Sanctuary Private Limited, which contributed Rs 10 crore. title: âShe would  be sitting on the bench againâ: Gujarat Giants explain Danni Wyatt-Hodge release
text: England's Danni Wyatt-Hodge celebrates reaching her century. (AP Photo) Mumbai: Gujarat Giants retained a large chunk of their squad ahead of the 2027 Women's Premier League player auction, a departure from the second season when they released 11 players. But they surprised by letting go of England batter Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who finished as the top run-scorer in the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup in England. Wyatt-Hodge scored 302 runs in seven matches at 60.40, including a century and two fifties, at a strike rate of 149.50, helping England reach the final. Gujarat Giants head coach Michael Klinger said Wyatt-Hodge was released because she was likely to spend much of WPL 2027 on the bench, with England also having commitments during the tournament. "As you would have seen last year, she didn't quite fit into our four overseas lineup for the majority of the time. I felt for her. She came in for one game and started reasonably well, getting about 12 or 15. Then she got sick just before the next game and was left out. Georgia Wareham came back in and had a really good game, and we stuck with that middle order all round option. "This year, England have commitments during the WPL. If we went with a similar setup, she would probably be sitting on the bench again. I spoke to both her and her representative, and they are keen for her to play some cricket during that time, leading into the Champions Trophy. I'm not sure whether she will enter the auction, but she was quite keen to play that England series around the same time. So for both parties, this was the best way to go. It also gives us another option in the auction, either the same skill set or a different one," Klinger said at an interaction on Thursday. Titas release Klinger said injury concerns also contributed to the decision to release India pacer Titas Sadhu, who has played 20 white-ball internationals. "What probably went against her this time was her injuries. She had an injury last season where we didn't really get a chance to see her, and she has been injured since. She is just making her comeback now. "We are having a training camp at the moment and we still asked her to come so we could have a look at her before the auction. She is progressing well and will start the domestic season on the 26th of October. Releasing her gives us a few more options in the auction. There is no reason we may not look to get her back, but it also gives us a chance to look at other options," he said. Fast-bowling depth Klinger believes India's domestic fast-bowling pool has improved, though the real test will come against international batters. âOverall, domestically, I think fast bowling is the area where Indian cricket can keep building depth. There has been a big change from when I started in this role a few years ago. The fast bowlers around the country are physically better. When you watch them bowl and field, they are fitter, more versatile, move better and are more agile. "That is only going to help them maintain pace and aggression for longer periods without injury. So I think Indian cricket is definitely on the right track in building depth in fast bowling. The test is always when they come up against international batters, whether that's international Indian batters or overseas batters in the WPL, because a lot of these bowlers haven't done that before. That's always the biggest test when they get on the big stage,â Klinger said. Giants target bowling consistency After missing the playoffs in their first two seasons, Gujarat Giants have reached the knockout stage in the last two. Klinger, who is overseeing an off-season camp in Bengaluru ahead of the October 28 auction in Kochi, identified bowling consistency as an area for improvement. "To be honest, we just had a bad final against Delhi Capitals. We beat them twice during the season in close games and didn't bring our best in that eliminator. That was disappointing, because I felt we probably had a stronger season than DC did throughout the year. But that's what finals are about. You need your best players to step up, and we probably didn't." "I think we can get more consistency with our bowling. Looking at the data and statistical information from last season, that's one area where we can improve. We have the personnel, and a couple of players are putting their hand up to get opportunities there this year, which will help us get some more quality overs. "Last year we defended some really big scores, but they were pretty tight games, and we also chased some big scores. I feel our batting is strong. If we can tighten up our bowling at certain times, then we'll be fine," he added. Anushka, Happy in focus Klinger backed Anushka Sharma after her impressive first WPL season and said her experience of international cricket could provide extra motivation. "Anushka Sharma was fantastic for us last year in her first WPL season. She has had a really good ODI series against Australia A and had a taste of international cricket. She probably could have been kept a little longer with more opportunities there, but I'm hoping that works in our favour. "Having tasted international cricket, I'm sure she will be desperate to do everything she can to get back. Both she and Yastika (Bhatia, who too will play for GG in WPL-2027) are in the same boat, playing for India at the moment. title: California tech company owner arrested over alleged $300 million China chip-smuggling scheme
text: Greg Lui, 38, was arrested after being charged in a three-count federal indictment. A California technology company owner has been arrested on charges of allegedly smuggling more than USD 300 million in export-controlled computer servers containing US-made graphics processing units (GPUs) to China, according to federal prosecutors. The US Department of Justice said Greg Lui, 38, also known as Yiu Kong Lui, was arrested after being charged in a three-count federal indictment. Lui, who owns City of Industry-based Earthmade Computer Inc., allegedly used third countries, false paperwork and freight-forwarding arrangements to send restricted technology to China without the required US export licences. According to the indictment, the alleged scheme operated between 2023 and 2024. Lui and his co-conspirators allegedly bought export-controlled servers through Earthmade and routed them to countries including Malaysia and Singapore, where the required US export licence was not needed, before arranging for the equipment to be re-exported to China. Prosecutors allege the servers contained high-end GPUs used for Super Intelligence (SI) computing. Lui allegedly knew that the actual end users were in China while providing US manufacturers with documents showing permitted destinations and end users. The indictment alleges that Lui and his associates used freight-forwarding companies to move the servers from the US to third countries before they were sent on to China. From January to October 2024, Earthmade allegedly received more than $176 million from two Malaysia-based shipment companies. In one instance cited by prosecutors, Lui placed an order in January 2024 for 27 servers worth about $7.6 million. The servers were shipped from Los Angeles to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. A subsequent email to a Malaysian government official allegedly indicated that the 27 servers had been transshipped to a China-based buyer. Lui faces charges of conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and Export Administration Regulations, outbound smuggling and conspiracy to commit money laundering. The FBI, the Defence Criminal Investigative Service and the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security Office of Export Enforcement are investigating the case. title: California man arrested on charges of smuggling banned Nvidia chips to China; follows arrest of Super Micro Computer founder, may face 20 years in jail
text: Representative image A California man has been arrested over alleged chip smuggling. The 38-year-old owner of San Gabriel Valley-based Earthmade Computer Inc. is accused of smuggling more than $300 million worth of export-controlled computer servers containing US-manufactured graphics processing units (GPUs) to China. Prosecutors allege that Greg Lui, also known as âYiu Kong Luiâ, used false paperwork and routed the high-end servers through countries including Malaysia and Singapore before they were allegedly re-exported to China. The case follows US authorities' separate arrest of Super Micro Computer co-founder Yih-Shyan âWallyâ Liaw in connection with an alleged scheme to divert Nvidia-powered AI servers to China. If convicted of all three charges, Lui could face up to 20 years in prison on the conspiracy and money laundering counts and up to 10 years on the smuggling count. California man accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to China Lui is charged with one count of conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and Export Administration Regulations, one count of outbound smuggling and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering. âSI is the defining technology of the era,â said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. âThe National Security Division will protect the American advantage in the chips that power this technology, a product of our unparalleled innovation and hard work, from illegal diversion by our economic and military adversaries.â According to an indictment returned on Sept. 29, Lui allegedly used Earthmade to buy export-controlled items between 2023 and 2024 and send them to China without required US licences. Prosecutors allege that the equipment was first shipped to Malaysia and Singapore before being re-exported to China. They also allege that Lui provided false documentation to US manufacturers, misrepresenting the intended end users and destinations. From January to October 2024, Earthmade received more than $176 million from two Malaysia-based shipment companies as part of the alleged scheme. How the alleged scheme worked In January 2024, Lui allegedly emailed a conspirator about a Malaysian transshipment company seeking 70 servers with export-restricted GPUs. Later that month, he allegedly ordered 27 servers from a US manufacturer for approximately $7.614 million. The servers were shipped from Los Angeles to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, with documents identifying their GPUs as export-controlled equipment that could not be sent to China without a licence. In March 2024, a co-conspirator allegedly told a Malaysian government official that the 27 servers had been transshipped to a China-based buyer. âProtecting Americaâs national security means keeping our advanced Super Intelligence technology from being used to strengthen our adversariesâ military capabilities,â said First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. âThis defendant allegedly used false paperwork and shipments through third countries to smuggle more than $300 million in export-controlled computer servers to China. We will aggressively prosecute those who put our national security at risk for profit.â FBI warns over advanced AI technology âThe FBIâs investigation revealed that Lui allegedly sold the Chinese government hundreds of millions of dollarsâ worth of American Super Intelligence technology, in clear violation of U.S. export control laws,â said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBIâs Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. âControlling the export of advanced SI technology is critical to safeguarding our national security and defending the homeland, and the FBI will keep fighting for Americaâs businesses and economic security. Weâre grateful to our partners across the U.S. government and private sector for their assistance, and weâll continue holding accountable anyone who violates U.S. export laws to enrich themselves and help our adversaries.â âPreventing the illegal export of controlled technology is critical to protecting our national security,â said Special Agent in Charge John E. Helsing of the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS) Western Field Office. âThese technologies provide core advantages to U.S. forces, and ensuring they remain safeguarded prevents adversaries from exploiting them. Todayâs action underscores our commitment to protecting advanced defense capabilities and enforcing the laws that keep them out of the hands of those who may threaten the United States.â Lui could face up to 20 years in prison If convicted of all charges, Lui could face a maximum of 20 years in prison on the conspiracy count, 20 years on the money laundering count and 10 years on the smuggling count. The Bureau of Industry and Security, Defense Criminal Investigative Service and FBI are investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Colin S. Scott and Joseph S. title: India's golden Saturday at Asian Games: Hockey, cricket, wrestling, golf and archery deliver golds
text: India's medal tally now stands at 85 medals â 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. The men's hockey team capped the day by beating Malaysia 5-1 in the final to retain their Asian Games title and book a place at the 2028 Olympics. India's medal tally now stands at 85 medals - 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. Watch Asmita Dey Unfiltered: Favourite Food, Match-Day Music & More | Rapid Fire | TOISA The victory gave India their fifth Asian Games men's hockey gold, after previous triumphs in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022. Harmanpreet became the first Indian men's hockey captain to lead the team to two Asian Games gold medals. The triumph came a day after the women's team beat defending champions China 1-0 to win their first Asian Games gold in 44 years and secure an Olympic berth. It was the first time that both Indian hockey teams finished on top of the podium at the same Asian Games. Aman wins wrestling gold, Antim settles for silver Aman Sehrawat upgraded his bronze from the 2023 Hangzhou Games to gold by beating North Korea's reigning world champion Chong Song Han 10-7 in the men's 57kg final. The 23-year-old was initially frustrated by Han's defensive approach but took control after being put on the clock. He built a 6-1 lead before Han fought back to move 7-6 ahead. Aman responded with two more takedowns to seal the gold. It was India's second wrestling gold of the Games after Sujeet Kalkal's title on Friday. India finished the wrestling competition with six medals â two gold, two silver and two bronze. Abhishek Sharma smashed 61 off 28 balls, hitting seven sixes, while Tilak Varma produced an unbeaten 51 off 22 balls as India posted 211/6. Pakistan fought back through Hasan Nawaz, who scored 96 off 51 balls, but India held their nerve to restrict them to 192/6. The victory also extended India's head-to-head dominance over Pakistan to 6-0 since the start of the 2024 T20 World Cup. title: In 2026, Phoenix added 19 shade roofs at busy crossings; the desert-inspired structures now give pedestrians a cooler place to wait for traffic lights
text: AI-generated representative image showing a desert-inspired shade canopy giving pedestrians relief while they wait at a crosswalk. Credits - Gemini In July, a red pedestrian light in Phoenix is a little endurance test. The sun beats down on your neck, the pavement is hot, and many places lack trees or cover. The city's solution, completed in April 2026, consists of 19 colorful shade structures installed at major intersections and crosswalks, where pedestrians can use them while waiting for traffic signals to change. The designs take inspiration from the Sonoran Desert. The City of Phoenix states the Office of Heat Response and Mitigation partnered with the Streets Transportation Department and the Department of Arts and Culture on the project. The locations were selected for pedestrians who must wait for traffic signals to change. Designs inspired by the desert Three different shade designs were used, all inspired by the local desert environment. Two are variations on the saguaro blossom, one a single panel by artist Isaac Caruso, the other a multi-panel rendition by Heidi Dauphin with Studio Curiosity. The third is a butterfly design by Sara Altieri of Green Heart Creative Services. Each structure has its own look, shaped by the artistsâ patterns etched in the roof panels and their choice of colour. The city's location list identifies structures with concrete bases as well as structures without them. The structures are distributed across the city, from Indian School Road and Central Avenue to Van Buren Street and 28th Street, and from Camelback Road and 23rd Avenue to Southern Avenue and 19th Avenue. The city had a public meeting in August 2024 to share plans and hear feedback. The project was not without its detractors. The project was funded with federal American Rescue Plan Act money, and Heat Response and Mitigation Director David Hondula said the funding requirements helped determine where structures could be installed. Councilwoman Betty Guardado expressed disappointment that District 5 would receive only one structure. The importance of shade in this context Itâs not easy to dismiss the health argument. In 2025, the yearly report of the Maricopa County public health department found 430 deaths attributable to heat. Itâs down from 608 in 2024 and a record 645 in 2023, but itâs still a terrible toll. That wonât be prevented by a shade canopy at a crossing by itself, but itâs aimed at a place where people canât just walk away from the sun. AI-generated representative image showing pedestrians waiting in the shade of a permanent canopy at an intersection during summer heat. Credits - GeminiÂ How much difference does it make Shade science tells us the roofs are worth the effort. Air temperature doesnât vary much between sun and shade, but what a body feels does. Air temperature may vary by only a couple of degrees between sun and shade, but physiological equivalent temperature, a measure of how hot conditions feel to the body, can vary by about 20 degrees in summer, said ASU urban climatologist Ariane Middel. She said constructed shade structures work in ASU studies for regions where trees have a particularly difficult time growing and donât need water. But shade is not a complete solution to extreme heat. An ASU field study led by Middel found that shade from photovoltaic canopies and trees improved outdoor thermal comfort in Tempe, showing why reducing direct solar exposure matters even when the surrounding air remains hot. The project covers only a small part of Phoenix's pedestrian network, while trees remain important to the city's longer-term shade strategy. The crossings provide relief at that one place where pedestrians have to pause in the sun, subject to the signal. That is a modest change that can help pedestrians crossing Phoenix in the summer. text: Arshpreet Singh & Vikramjeet Singh convicted In US cargo theft case/Image: FBILosAngles Two Indian nationals have been found guilty in the US of conspiring to steal cargo by using legitimate trucking companies to secure shipping contracts and then taking the goods without delivering them to their intended destinations. According to the US Attorneyâs Office for the Central District of California, Arshpreet Singh, 28, of Sacramento, and Vikramjeet Singh, 31, of Fontana, were found guilty after a seven-day jury trial. Prosecutors said the conspiracy operated from March 2024 to June 2025. Singh and his co-conspirators allegedly acquired established trucking companies or fraudulently used them to obtain genuine shipping contracts. After collecting the cargo, they allegedly kept the goods instead of completing the deliveries. The stolen shipments included televisions, laptops, appliances and other high-value consumer goods. Vacuums, LED lights, shoes and tyres were also taken, with the losses estimated at at least $2 million. The thefts occurred across Southern California, including Fontana, Vernon, Santa Fe Springs, Perris, City of Industry, Long Beach, Compton, Commerce, Pico Rivera, Chino and Moreno Valley. A shipment was also stolen in Grand Prairie, Texas. In one case, Arshpreet Singh allegedly agreed to buy Texas-based carrier Z&F Transportation LLC for about $22,000 in March 2024. Later that month, a co-conspirator acting for the company collected a shipment of televisions in Fontana that was meant for delivery to Florida but never reached its destination. Another trucking company, Skyways Trucking LLC, was purchased by co-conspirators in May 2024, prosecutors said. Loads including laptops, televisions and solar panels were subsequently booked through freight brokers, including Uber Freight, before the cargo was allegedly taken instead of delivered. Vikramjeet Singh was acquitted of a separate charge of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. US District Judge Anne Hwang has scheduled sentencing for January 20 next year. title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to replace Tilak Varma or Shivam Dube in âsix monthsâ, predicts ex-India cricketer
text: Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (PTI Photo) Mohammad Kaif believes India could face a major selection headache in the T20I format within the next six months, with the former batter predicting that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will force his way into the first-choice side. Kaif feels the teenage sensationâs emergence could eventually leave either Tilak Varma or Shivam Dube fighting for a place in the playing XI, despite Tilak currently being Indiaâs vice-captain. Watch Washington Sundar: India eye Asian Games gold after Japan preparations âI understand that Tilak is the vice-captain. But vice-captains have also been dropped before. I do not want to go there. Shivam Dube is not scoring in every game and still has to prove himself. Fielding is also his weakness, and he is not a proper bowling all-rounder. He is only playing as a batter. After six months, either Tilak or Dube will be out. You will have to remove one, and Sooryavanshi will play. I am saying this right now", Kaif said on his YouTube channel. Kaif pointed to Sooryavanshiâs performances beyond T20Is as another reason for his prediction. The teenager also made an impact in the Duleep Trophy and even bowled during the tournament, adding another dimension to his game. âSooryavanshi scored in the Duleep Trophy as well. He has improved his game. He was even bowling there. So he has understood that if he can bowl a few overs, he will have an advantage,â he added. The numbers behind Sooryavanshiâs rapid rise are difficult to overlook. In his first six T20Is of 2026, he has scored 193 runs at an average of 32.17 and a strike rate of 189.22. He has found the boundary once every 3.4 deliveries and hit a six every 7.2 balls. His IPL campaign strengthened that case further. Sooryavanshi finished the season with 776 runs at an average of 48.50 and a strike rate of 237.51, including 72 sixes. Those numbers have already shifted the conversation around the teenager. Rather than being viewed solely as a young player being gradually introduced to international cricket, Sooryavanshi is increasingly making a case for a regular place in Indiaâs T20I setup. Tilakâs numbers, meanwhile, remain respectable on the surface. He has scored 395 runs in T20Is in 2026 at an average of 35.91 and a strike rate of 154.90. However, the timing of some of those runs adds another layer to the debate. His fifty came in the fifth and final T20I against England, by which point India had already lost the series, and India went on to lose that match as well. Another notable contribution came during the Zimbabwe tour, although the quality of the opposition bowling was not necessarily of the highest pedigree. There have also been occasions when Tilak has found it difficult to rotate the strike after being promoted up the order or arriving at the crease earlier than expected, particularly against spin. At the other end of the innings, however, he has shown greater effectiveness as a finisher, including against Jofra Archer. That creates a contrast in the type of batter India could eventually have to choose between. Sooryavanshi represents an extreme-tempo approach built around relentless boundary-hitting, while Tilak offers greater adaptability and the ability to construct an innings. Dubeâs numbers also make the selection debate more complicated than Kaifâs assessment might suggest. The all-rounder has scored 415 T20I runs in 2026 at an average of 31.92 and a strike rate of 170.78. At the T20 World Cup, he scored 235 runs at a strike rate of 169.06, giving India substantial returns from a player primarily selected for his power-hitting. Those figures underline how India have largely used him as a batter who can provide occasional overs rather than as a genuine bowling all-rounder. Had we played that day, things would have been different. But next morning, fresh new ball attack. They got the best of the conditions and they put us under attack and they banked on the hesitation that we had. âThat was too tough to swallow and process. I was distraught. text: Rohit Sharma Sunil Gavaskar was disappointed to see Rohit Sharma miss out on an ODI century in the third match against the West Indies, saying he wants the Indian opener to finish his international career with more ODI hundreds than his age.
