title: Kochiâs urban footprint expands as coastal wetlands shrink
text: City's built-up area rose 48% in two decades as the wider coastal stretch saw a 239% increase An aerial view of waterfront development between Marine Drive and Chathiyath Road in Kochi Kochi: Urbanisation has surged in the Kochi Corporation area over the last 20 years. Between 2004 and 2024, built-up area here rose 48% from 42.86 sqkm to 63.26 sqkm, increasing risks of urban heat, waterlogging and pollution for humans and other living organisms. The finding is from a study jointly conducted by National Centre for Earth Science Studies, Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies, Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology in Chennai and KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Sweden, which notes that high urbanisation in and around the corporation limits, such as North Paravoor, Tripunithura and Kalamassery, could pose a significant challenge to authorities and residents. It is causing a gradual decline of natural and semi-natural coastal land cover, which can accelerate coastal erosion and shoreline shifting and increase vulnerability to natural disasters, even resulting in habitat loss. The study examined land use and land cover changes along the coastal alluvial soil stretch (marine-origin soil found along coastal plains), covering 461 sqkm in Ernakulam and 1,222 sqkm in Alappuzha. It projects 100% growth in built-up area here in three decades, by 2054. The study examined land use and land cover changes along the coastal alluvial soil stretch (marine-origin soil found along coastal plains), covering 461 sqkm in Ernakulam and 1,222 sqkm in Alappuzha Built-up area along the stretch has increased by 240%, from 109.93 sqkm in 2004 to 373.49 sqkm in 2024, largely at the expense of plantation, vegetation, wetland and agricultural land. The study also shows high urbanisation leads to declining vegetation and wetlands, alongside an increase in waterlogged areas. âKochi Corporation emerges as the most urbanized, with its built-up area increasing... It is followed by urban centres such as Alappuzha, Mavelikkara, Kayamkulam, Ambalapuzha, Cherthala, Thrikkakara and North Paravoor. Such expansion of settlements, particularly along the coast, has resulted in large-scale encroachment of coastal land cover, intensifying ecosystem degradation and coastal vulnerability,â the study warns. âAll existing buildings in Kochi are situated in wetland reclaimed lands. When the built-up area increases, there is possibility for soil subsidence in future. Besides, the growing urbanisation will lead to intensified urban flooding as there wonât be enough permeable soil to pave way for the infiltration of water,â said Prof Girish Gopinath of Kufos, who was part of the study. It also shows declining sandy beaches, a major protector of coasts. âBeach erosion and accretion are natural processes. But erosion is happening more now due to anthropogenic activities like construction of groynes, breakwaters, ports and other structures making the coasts vulnerable to high erosion amid climate change,â he said. Urban policy experts note that compact urbanisation in Kerala, which is sandwiched between the coast and the Western Ghats, can happen in the midland, and that too at linear level. âWe follow a market driven urbanisation approach in the state where there is not enough land space. What we need is a scientific approach by studying the carrying capacity of places in midland. The govt has to take a lead in this regard. As we are facing climate change related hazards both in coastal and high lands, midland is the only option available for us for ensuring safe living. But it should be done scientifically as Nature is letting us know that Kerala is not suitable for large population and unscientific urban expansion,â said an urban policy expert. text: Police said five face deportation proceedings, while a case was registered against one for allegedly facilitating their entry, accommodation and employment Mumbai: Khar policeâs Anti-Terrorism Cell on Tuesday arrested six Bangladeshi nationals, including three women, for allegedly entering India illegally and staying in Bhayander without valid documents. title: Metro suspends services at 12 stations, commuters impacted
text: New Delhi: Metro services at 12 stations in central Delhi were suspended Friday, causing severe inconvenience to commuters. Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) did not give any official reason for the sudden closure that came on a day protests at Jantar Mantar were planned. At 8 am, DMRC announced on social media that the entry and exit at 11 metro stations would remain closed till further notice. They are Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Rajiv Chowk, Seva Teerth, Mandi House, Lok Kalyan Marg, INA, Chawri Bazaar, Ramakrishna Ashram Marg and New Delhi. âHowever, interchange facility will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, INA, New Delhi and Central Secretariat stations,â it added. Four hours later, Barakhambha Road station was added to the list. Around 2 pm, DMRC posted that the interchange facility at New Delhi Metro station, a key link between Yellow and Airport Express lines, wouldnât be available till further notice. Many commuters complained that the closure of the stations left them scrambling for alternative routes to reach their destinations. While educational institutions and govt offices remained shut because of Gandhi Jayanti, many private offices, coaching centres and shops were open. Rashi Sharma, whose office is in Janpath, said the disruption added to her travel time. âSince the metro did not stop at Janpath or the next station, Mandi House, I had to get off at ITO and take an auto from there,â she said. Mahesh Singh, who works at a shop in Connaught Place, said, âI requested security personnel at Rajiv Chowk to allow me to exit from one of the gates. However, they didnât listen to me.â Many commuters took to social media to complain about the disruption. Nitesh, a passenger, wrote on X, âI have a train to catch from New Delhi railway station. How am I supposed to reach there? Why should I compromise?â Another X user, Vaibhav, whose train did not stop at some stations on Yellow Line, said, âWhy didnât you announce this yesterday?â DMRC sources said the closure followed directions from police regarding locations identified by them as sensitive from security and law-and-order perspectives. A senior police officer echoed this, saying the step came after the situation and security measures were assessed. The closure of metro stations as a precautionary measure during protests in Delhi has been a recurring feature in recent years. During the CJP stir in July, 18 metro stations in central Delhi were shut for days. In Feb 2024, multiple gates at nine metro stations across the city were closed in view of a farmersâ stir. In Jan 2021, 16 stations were shut after protesting farmers entered the city and clashes erupted near Red Fort and ITO. During the height of anti-CAA and NRC protests in 2019, DMRC temporarily closed nearly 20 stations. title: India withstand Hasan Nawaz onslaught to beat Pakistan, win Asian Games gold
text: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games menâs T20 final to claim gold after posting 211/6 and restricting Pakistan to 192. (Image: Reuters) TimesofIndia in Aichi-Nagoya : The warm hugs, high-fives and handshakes that have become a norm between Indian and Pakistani athletes across sports at the Asian Games took a leave of absence when the cricket teams played at the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin on Saturday. Enter Shreyas Iyer and his men. There were no customary courtesies, only an expression of rivalry and an unmistakable desire to win gold. By the time the sun set over the Owari Hills, the gold medal was glistening around the necks of Iyer and his men. But Pakistan had ensured it was no procession, launching a late fightback that put the champagne on ice for the defending champions. Opting to bat, India rode on half-centuries from Abhishek Sharma (61; 28b, 3x4, 7x6) and Tilak Varma (51*; 22b, 2x4, 4x6) to post 211/6. Pakistan, reduced to 31/3 at the end of the Powerplay, appeared headed for a heavy defeat. Then Hasan Nawaz took charge, smashing a breathtaking 51-ball 96 (5x4, 7x6). But his assault came too late as Pakistan finished on 192/6, handing India a 19-run victory. On a surface that played differently from the one used in the semifinals, Indiaâs openers took a little time to settle in. Pakistanâs decision to open with off-spinner Saim Ayub looked like a good move but the bubble burst soon after as Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek soon found their range. Sooryavanshi provided the early fireworks, dropping to one knee to launch leg-spinner Saad Masood over the bowlerâs head before pulling the next delivery through midwicket. Abhishek was not to be outdone, finding the region beyond mid-on. While Sooryavanshi and Sanju Samson returned to the makeshift dressing room, Abhishek, who survived a dropped catch and a run-out, tormented the Pakistan attack as India raced to 81 in the Powerplay. Length was a major issue for Pakistan, who repeatedly bowled short to the in-form batters. Once they got that right, there was a lull of almost six overs without a boundary before Tilak and Shivam Dube launched the late assault. The final push came in the penultimate over, which yielded 23 runs and propelled India beyond 200. With Pakistan 31/3 after six overs, an early finish seemed on the cards. Hasan Nawaz had other ideas. The right-hander produced an innings to remember, keeping Pakistan in the contest almost single-handedly. But by then, India had done enough to ensure the gold stayed with them. For Iyer, the victory was also a reward for a team that had refused to let circumstances derail its campaign. But the boys prepped themselves and we trained on the side. We didnât complain, we didnât give any reason,â Iyer said. âThat was a sign of a champion team and today was just a reflection of that,â he added. title: Row over shifting flights to Navi Mumbai airport and T1 redevelopment: Civil Aviation Ministry to meet airlines and Mumbai International Airport Ltd on Oct 6
text: Navi Mumbai international airport New Delhi: Union civil aviation secretary Samir Sinha has called a meeting of airlines and Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) on Tuesday to find an amicable solution to the impasse over shifting some flights to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) and beginning phase-wise redevelopment of Mumbai airport terminal 1 (T1). T1 has been built in phases over six decades, with T1B dating to 1965, T1A to 1992 and T1C to 2010. MIAL plans to begin redevelopment with the oldest portion, citing structural safety concerns. Airlines have resisted splitting operations between Mumbaiâs two airports. Air France-KLM GM India Stefan Gumuseli said last week: âFrom an efficiency perspective, we have teams on the ground (at Mumbai), and to split, we need to have new teams. There will be more challenges to train (people). From that perspective, splitting is not an option.â Concerns over T1âs structural condition date back nearly a decade. A 2017 structural audit of T1B found severe corrosion in some areas, including spalling concrete, exposed and snapped reinforcement and cracks. It said the affected areas could create âserious concernsâ and advised demolition. An AERA tariff consultation paper in September 2020 had also noted MIALâs submission that T1B had âbecome structurally weakâ, while acknowledging the projectâs necessity from the standpoint of structural safety. The planned reconstruction was deferred amid the Covid-19 pandemic. Officials are now concerned that deterioration may have worsened over the years. The collapse of a canopy at Delhi airport during heavy rain in June 2024, which killed one person, has added to concerns about ageing airport structures. title: Mumbai Police arrest 6 Bangladeshi nationals for illegal entry
text: Police said deportation proceedings had been initiated against five of them. MUMBAI: The Khar police's Anti-Terrorism Cell (ATC) arrested six Bangladeshi nationals, including three women, on September 29 for allegedly entering India illegally and staying in Bhayandar without valid passports, travel documents or visas. Police said deportation proceedings had been initiated against five of them, while a case was registered against Iqbal Akbarali Shaikh alias Gautam Sunil Datta (35) under Section 24 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. He is accused of facilitating their entry into India, arranging accommodation and helping them find employment. The six were detained around 3pm after police found them behaving suspiciously near Bandra Traffic Chowki on SV Road. An officer recognised some of them from earlier action against illegal immigration. According to police, four of the six had previously been deported to Bangladesh. Besides Iqbal, those arrested were Rana Molla Imdadul Molla alias Rana Shah (20), Samim Mizanur Sardar alias Raju Narendra (25), Mosamod Munjila Khatun alias Sila Sardar alias Riya Datta (23), Mafuja Akthar Lima alias Kavita Shah (25), and Halima Akthar alias Monica Datta (26). Police recovered photocopies of Bangladeshi identity documents or a birth certificate from the accused and seized four mobile phones, each valued at Rs 5,000. During questioning, Iqbal allegedly told police that he had been travelling between Bangladesh and India for around five years. Police records also revealed that he was out on bail in an earlier case related to his alleged illegal entry and stay in India. Halima reportedly told investigators that she had entered India around six months ago with Iqbal's assistance. The other four allegedly said they had crossed the Bangladesh border on September 20 without valid documents and paid Iqbal, whose associates had helped them enter the country. Police said Iqbal subsequently put the five in touch with agents who arranged accommodation for them at the Golden Nest and Geeta Sarovar buildings in Bhayandar and helped them secure jobs. They were allegedly employed as labourers, domestic workers and beauty parlour staff. Deportation proceedings against the five have been initiated, and police are also seeking orders to restrict their movement until they are deported. DCP (Mumbai Crime) Raj Tilak Roshan said 1,066 Bangladeshi nationals allegedly staying illegally in India had been deported up to the end of August 2026, compared with 1,061 in 2025 and 164 in 2024. Since 2024, Mumbai Police have registered 658 cases and arrested 995 people allegedly residing illegally in the city. The Indiana Fever veteran said Clark and Reese have helped open new doors for womenâs basketball and brought more attention to the league. Mitchell, who has played alongside Clark since the Fever drafted her in 2024, spoke about the pair in her recent SLAM cover story. Her comments come as the WNBA continues to see strong interest around its biggest young names, with Clark and Reese playing a major part in that wider conversation. Kelsey Mitchell explains Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese impact Clark and Reese entered the WNBA in 2024 after being two of the biggest names in college basketball. Their rivalry from college followed them into the league, and games involving the two quickly became major draws. The numbers from that season showed just how much interest the WNBA was getting. According to the WNBA, the league recorded its highest total attendance in 22 years in 2024, with 2,353,735 fans attending games. Total attendance was up 48% from the previous season, while the league recorded 154 sellouts. Mitchell sees that growth as something the league should embrace. Rather than treating new stars as a threat to established players, she believes their arrival can create more opportunities for everyone involved in womenâs basketball. âYou canât gatekeep,â Mitchell said. âIt would only pigeonhole our game. When Angel Reese and CC came in â¦ it opened up so many doors for us.â The comments were made in Mitchellâs interview with SLAM, where she discussed the changing WNBA and the effect of a new group of young players. SLAM also shared a clip of Mitchell discussing her views on the leagueâs growth. Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell have built Fever partnership Mitchell has had a close view of Clarkâs WNBA career from the beginning. The two have been teammates in Indiana since Clark arrived as the No. 1 pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft. By 2026, both had become All-Stars, with Mitchell selected as a 2026 All-Star starter alongside Clark. Their partnership has also become an important part of the Feverâs offense. title: Stateâs alcohol revenue dependence among highest, growth among slowest
text: Hyderabad: Telangana derives a larger share of its own-tax revenue from alcohol than several major states, even as growth in alcohol tax revenue has remained among the slowest, according to a Telangana government revenue brief. According to analysis by the industry sources, alcohol accounted for 31.8% of Telangana's own-tax revenue in 2024-25, the highest among states shown in the comparison. Tamil Nadu followed at 26.9%, Uttar Pradesh at 24.7%, Andhra Pradesh at 23.8%, Kerala at 22.4% and Karnataka at 20.4%. The share was lower in Rajasthan at 18.8%, Haryana at 17.2%, Maharashtra at 11.7% and Jharkhand at 12.8%. However, Telangana recorded only 5.9% growth in alcohol tax revenue between FY22 and FY26, placing it at the bottom of the comparison. Andhra Pradesh recorded 5.1%, while Kerala registered 7.4% growth. Several other states recorded considerably faster growth. Maharashtra's alcohol tax revenue grew 24.7% during the period, followed by Chhattisgarh at 21.5%, Odisha 20%, Rajasthan 16.1%, Uttar Pradesh 13.6%, Karnataka 12% and Tamil Nadu 11.1%. The figures point to a significant dependence on alcohol-related revenue in Telanganaâs tax structure, while the relatively modest growth indicates that collections have expanded slowly compared with other states. The revenue brief notes that recent revenue growth came largely through price and mix, with volume growth at only 1.6%. It also points to structural factors such as number of outlets, brands, pricing and taxation as areas that influence alcohol revenue. title: HPV Vaccination for adolescents: What parents need to know
text: Talking to your teenager about sensitive topics like intercourse and cancer can be uncomfortable for many parents. It is a conversation that most of us would much rather avoid. But these discussions become necessary when it comes to protecting your childâs health against cervical cancer. HPV vaccination, screening and lifestyle related changes can help protect against cervical cancer and certain HPV related cancers and diseases. Here's everything you need to know about HPV vaccination, why it is so important for adolescents and address any common concerns that you may have. What is HPV? HPV stands for Human Papilloma Virus, a common virus that affects both males and females. It is primarily spread through intimate skin-to-skin contact. While many HPV infections are harmless and go away on their own, certain types can lead to more serious health problems, such as cancers of the cervix, and genital areas [1] . The virus is highly prevalent, and most sexually active people come into contact with it at some point in their lives. Health risks of HPV HPV is responsible for various health complications. In women, cervical cancer is the second most common cancer in women aged 15-44 years. Additionally, WHO also claims that 95% of persistent high risk HPV infection in the cervix leads to cervical cancer [3] . The risk of these cancers and HPV related diseases highlights the importance of taking preventive measures, such as HPV vaccination. Prevalence of HPV and Cervical Cancer in India. Health problems associated with HPV are increasing. In India, among women aged 15 to 44, cervical cancer is the second most common cancer, according to a 2023 report by the HPV Information Centre [4] . With these statistics, we understand that health problems associated with HPV are a major concern in India. This also increases the worry about the prevalence of HPV among teenagers and young adults. Importance of HPV Vaccination in adolescents HPV vaccination is one of the highly recommended ways by pediatricians and gynaecologists to help protect your child from certain risks associated with HPV. The primary role of HPV vaccination is that it provides protection against HPV by stimulating the bodyâs immune system to fight off the virus. HPV vaccination can help reduce the chances of your adolescent children developing certain HPV related diseases. Recommended age for HPV vaccination As per WHOâs guidelines, the preferable time to vaccinate your child against HPV is during their adolescent years, typically between ages 9 and 14 years [5] . When children receive HPV vaccination between 9-15 years, their immune system responds more strongly, producing nearly twice as many antibodies compared to when the vaccination is administered at a later age. Experts recommend vaccinating both boys and girls early starting 9 years, before any potential exposure to HPV. Efficacy of the HPV vaccination According to studies, HPV vaccination is effective against certain cancers caused by HPV depending on the vaccination HPV types [5] . Safety of HPV vaccination HPV vaccination generally has a good safety profile. It is available in more than 170 countries. There are over 135 million doses distributed worldwide. Common side effects of HPV vaccination HPV vaccination is generally well-tolerated. The side effects of the vaccination are mild and temporary, and they may include pain or swelling at the injection site, a low-grade fever, or mild headache [5] . These side effects are similar to reactions experienced with other standard routine vaccinations and usually resolve on their own within a day or two. Steps for getting your adolescent child vaccinated Consultation : The initial step is to consult with a pediatrician. They can provide you with detailed information about HPV vaccination. The doctor can also advise you on the right time to start the vaccination process. You can discuss your concerns during the consultation and get professional advice that aligns with your child's needs. Vaccination schedule [7] : HPV vaccination cycle usually consists of two or three shots, the number of shots depending on the age at which the vaccination begins. Consult your child's pediatrician for more information. Where to get the vaccination : HPV vaccination is available across various healthcare institutions. If you are unsure where to take your child for vaccination, consult your regular healthcare provider or reach out to a trusted medical professional. HPV vaccination is one of the important ways to help protect your child against risk of certain HPV related cancers and diseases. Contact your pediatrician to arrange your child's HPV vaccination. FAQs on HPV vaccination Q: How can I explain HPV vaccination to my child? A: Use simple terms that your child can easily understand. Explain to your child, stating that the vaccination will help protect them from getting sick from certain HPV related diseases, just like all other vaccinations they have had before. Q: Is HPV vaccination safe? A: Yes, HPV vaccination generally has a good safety profile. Just like other vaccinations, it can cause some mild and temporary side effects. NOTE : HPV - Human Papillomavirus. This information is intended for awareness purposes only and should not be considered a substitute for professional medical advice. Please consult your gynaecologist. HPV vaccination is not intended to be used for treatment and may not result in protection in all vaccination recipients. Vaccination does not eliminate the necessity for women to continue HPV relevant cancer screening recommended by their doctor. title: Late-Sept pollution spike pushes city AQI to 3-year high
text: Gurgaon's average AQI in September was 26% higher than in 2024 and about 35% higher than in 2025 Gurgaon: The average air quality index (AQI) last month was 26% higher than in 2024 and around 35% higher than in 2025, making it the cityâs most polluted Sept in three years. An analysis of daily AQI data from 2016 to 2026 shows that the monthly average rose to 114.8 this year, compared with 91.1 in 2024 and 84.9 in 2025. The rise was driven largely by a sharp decline in air quality in the second half of the month. After relatively moderate levels during the first 18 days, the city recorded a five-day spell of high pollution from Sept 20 to 24. The AQI crossed 200 on four of those days and touched the monthâs peak of 242 (poor) on Sept 22. The AQI stood at 195 on Sept 20, 218 on Sept 21, 242 on Sept 22, 214 on Sept 23 and 237 on Sept 24, with the five-day average at 221.2. The month had begun on a better note, with an AQI of 94 on Sept 1. It stayed below 140 for most of the first 18 days and dropped to 81 on Sept 18. It then climbed to 120 on Sept 19 and 195 the next day. The average AQI for the first 18 days was around 90, while the average between Sept 19 and 30 was 152, showing the extent to which the late-month deterioration pushed up the monthly figure. Residents said the change in air quality was noticeable on several days, particularly in the mornings and evenings. âWe have seen more dust and a layer of haze, even before the peak winter pollution season begins,â said Ashutosh Ahalawat, a resident of Sector 90. Gunjan Agarwal, a resident of Sector 53, said, âSept used to be relatively comfortable after the monsoon, but this year the air was very polluted. With GRAP coming into force from Oct 1, residents are worried about what the coming months will bring.â Rajesh Menon, a resident of Sector 57, said the AQI readings reflected what people were experiencing on the ground. âThe AQI numbers may fluctuate, but people can feel the difference. There is more dust on roads and the air feels heavier on some days. The concern is that if pollution is already rising in Sept, the situation could become much worse in winter,â he said. Air quality improved after Sept 24. The AQI fell to 140 on Sept 25, 90 on Sept 26 and 71 on Sept 27. It was 98 on Sept 28, 89 on Sept 29 and 114 on Sept 30. Despite the increase, Sept 2026 remained less polluted than some earlier years. The average AQI was 140.8 in 2023, 133.4 in 2017, 118.6 in 2022 and 117.7 in 2020. The corresponding averages were 91.9 in 2018, 70.3 in 2021, 67.7 in 2016 and 65.9 in 2019. The data indicates a reversal after two consecutive years of lower Sept AQI. The average had fallen from 140.8 in 2023 to 91.1 in 2024 and 84.9 in 2025 before rising to 114.8 this year. âThe rise in Sept AQI this year suggests that Gurgaonâs air quality has weakened compared with the last two years, but it is too early to conclude that the city is heading towards an exceptionally polluted winter. Sept 2026 marks a return to the moderate category after two years of satisfactory air quality, yet pollution levels remain below those recorded in several earlier years. At this stage, deterioration appears more consistent with a return to typical pre-winter conditions, potentially influenced by weather variability, than with a clear signal of an unusually challenging pollution season ahead,â said Jinitha Varghese, programme manager, EnviroCatalysts. Air quality experts said the late-Sept spike needs to be assessed against changes in meteorological conditions and the build-up of local and regional emissions. title: ILT20 Season 5 auction: $1.3 million in purse, rules and everything you need to know
text: Desert Vipers are reigning ILT20 champions. The ILT20 Season 5 Player Auction will be held in Dubai on October 1, with the tournament's six franchises looking to finalise their squads ahead of the 2026 season, which runs from November 21 to December 20. Following the pre-auction signings announced in August, teams will head into the auction with a $1.3 million purse, in addition to any unspent balance from the $700,000 allocated for direct signings and retentions. Each franchise must finish with a total squad spend between $1.5 million and $2 million. Watch ILT20: How India connect can help the league grow even further | Laxmi Shetty Interview Squad composition rules Franchises must assemble squads of 18 to 23 players, while adhering to strict nationality quotas designed to strengthen both Full Member and Associate cricket. Each squad must include a minimum of 11 players from ICC Full Member nations, including at least four Afghans and one Irish player. Teams are also required to sign four UAE players, one player each from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, and at least one additional Associate player from another ICC Associate nation. Auction mechanics and Right to Match ILT20 auction rules ahead of the fifth season that begins in November 2026. Players entered the auction with base prices of $10,000, $40,000 or $80,000, depending on their eligibility and international experience. UAE, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia players all carry a base price of $10,000. Bidding will begin at the player's base price before rising in increments of $2,000 up to $50,000, $5,000 between $50,000 and $100,000, and $10,000 thereafter. Each franchise will also have four optional Right to Match cards â one each for a Full Member player, an Associate player, a UAE player, and a Kuwait or Saudi Arabia player who represented the franchise in Season 4. title: Aidan Heslop feared his diving career was over after back surgery but 444 days later he returned to become a world champion again
text: Aidan Heslop feared his diving career was over after back surgery but 444 days later he returned to become a world champion again Aidan Heslop thought he might never dive again after a back injury kept him away from the 27-metre platform for 444 days. He had surgery, went through months of failed treatment and watched other divers compete while he struggled to recover. Almost two years after his injury first appeared, the British diver returned to the top in 2026. Heslop finished fourth at the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series final in Polignano a Mare, Italy, on September 27, which was enough to give him his second King Kahekili Trophy. Red Bull confirmed his championship after his comeback season. Aidan Heslopâs back injury turned a small pain into a major setback The problem started after Heslop won the 2024 World Series event in Boston. The next day, he felt a small pain in his glute, but thought it was ânothingâ. It later became a herniated disc and grew worse over the next few months. âIt slowly got worse and worse and worse until a point where I could barely even touch my toes,â Heslop told Daily Mail Sport. âI was getting pretty lucky with the diving, to be honest, that the judges werenât caning me on it. âAnd then in Sydney, that was really when it all blew up. From Boston to Sydney was a five-month period where it just got worse, and worse, and worse. Those competition days [in Sydney], I was drugged up to the gills. I didnât get any injections, but I had dry needling done, which was so painful.â Heslop still won the 2024 World Series title, but the injury meant he then faced a much longer battle. Several doctors advised more physiotherapy and injections, but neither solved the problem. âI was seeing a doctor, and they would tell me, âjust go do physioâ and I would go do some physio. And it wouldnât work. Then Iâd go back and theyâd say, âletâs do this cortisol steroid injectionâ. I would go and get it; nothing helped.â He eventually decided that surgery was the only option left. âIâd been to three doctors; I wanted the surgery at this point. I knew the alternatives werenât working. And theyâre like, âwe just need to try everything else, there is so much risk in surgeryâ. I knew there was, but I didnât see myself ever getting back to diving if I didnât get the surgery, and no one was giving it to me.â âThat was the point when it was in my head that I wouldnât be diving again.â Aidan Heslop returned to win his second world title The 444-day break was especially difficult because diving had been part of Heslopâs life since childhood. He had started diving after meeting Tom Daley at the age of six and later became the youngest man to compete in the Red Bull World Series. âIâve never not dived for more than a couple of months at a time, so not diving for that long was easily the biggest mental challenge Iâve ever been through.â After surgery and rehabilitation, Heslop returned to competition in 2026. He won in Bali and then built a strong lead across the following events before arriving in Polignano a Mare with the title within reach. Red Bull lists the Italian town as the final stop of the 2026 World Series. In a weird way, I kind of appreciate what happened.â He also changed his approach to training, saying he now spends much more time in the gym. âI donât really know how to feel,â Heslop admitted after lifting his second Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series trophy. âIâve never been in a situation like this. title: Holkar Stadium unveils royal makeover ahead of India-West Indies T20I
text: Indore : The cityâs Holkar Stadium is gearing up to give cricket fans a royal welcome ahead of the India-West Indies T20I on Oct 11, with its entrance gates and boundary walls undergoing a makeover. The stadiumâs gates are being redesigned around a fort-inspired theme, with a red-brick aesthetic similar to that of its existing museum, while the height and pattern of the outer walls are also being altered to give the venue a distinctive new look. âThe height of the walls is being increased, and their pattern is being changed to give the stadium a different appearance. The entrance gates have also been replaced, with their height increased as part of the redesign,â Madhya Pradesh Cricket Association (MPCA) secretary Sudhir Asnani told TOI. Repair work and improvements are underway inside the stadium alongside exterior changes. A special platform is being prepared for VIP spectators, dressing rooms are being renovated, and other facilities will be reviewed and completed before the match. The stadiumâs hospitality area has also been enhanced, with seating added in different sections. Around 250-300 seats have been added in this category. The preparations come amid strong ticket demand, with general-category tickets selling out within 113 minutes after online sales opened at 6 am on Sept 25. Holkar Stadium has hosted international cricket for nearly two decades, beginning with an India-England match in 2006. It has since staged Test, one-day international and T20 matches, besides Indian Premier League fixtures. The stadium has a legacy linked to the Holkar royal family, which provided land for the ground and promoted cricket in the region. The Holkar cricket team played 10 Ranji Trophy seasons, reaching eight finals and winning four titles. Several parts of the stadium have been named after prominent Indian cricketers. The pavilion honours former players Colonel C K Nayudu and Mushtaq Ali, while the dressing rooms are named after Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi and Rahul Dravid. Stands honour Vijay Hazare, Ajit Wadekar, Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev, Sachin Tendulkar and Anil Kumble. With entrance gates being renovated and internal improvements carried out, the stadium prepares to welcome a packed crowd for the Oct 11 fixture. title: Protector/predator
text: File photo Any alleged crime is more horrifying when the accused are in positions of trust. And victims have no voice â in this case, wildlife. Allegations swirling around animal-rescue NGO, Wildlife SOS, must be thoroughly investigated, and cases must not be allowed to linger. The NGO claims its intelligence network helps authorities detect wildlife crime. But cops are investigating whether the NGO, with several facilities in many states, has allegedly also taken part in wildlife crime. These allegations have redoubled after Madhya Pradeshâs tiger strike force traced leopard skins seized in neighbouring UP to the NGO staff. The probe has also circled back, to a 2022 case of 30kg of ivory seized, and elephant smuggling, in which NGO staff were reportedly named by those arrested. That Indian authorities are deeply worried is also evident in the fact that Central Zoo Authority, just days ago, asked chief wildlife wardens of six states and a UT to inspect Wildlife SOSâs facilities for allegedly violating Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. This law requires all such facilities to maintain records on provenance and number of animals. Rescued animals in NGO facilities risk becoming a bit of a problem area. What happens to such animals, in shelters that arenât CZA-authorised, is iffy â where are the records of provenance, as well as animal mortality and births? Per UNEP, illegal animal trade generates up to $23bn annually. A new investigation on online wildlife trafficking, by Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, found that Metaâs platforms, especially Facebook, had become a major marketplace for endangered animals and animal parts. Meta, of course, bans such sales, but the research identified over 20k ads offering over 2.6L wildlife products between Apr 2024 and March 2026. The animals were meant for illegal private collections, or for consumption or folk medicine. If a protector turns predator, only speedy probe and swift justice can be a deterrent. text: "Rahul Gandhi was reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Amethi," says Congress ally. NEW DELHI: Strain deepened within the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance ahead of Uttar Pradesh polls, with SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel in an off-the-cuff remark claimed that Rahul Gandhi was "reluctant to contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election" from Amethi and chose Raebareli because he was "so scared". Patel, who represents Pratapgarh, also credited the SP-Congress alliance for the Congress's six Lok Sabha wins in Uttar Pradesh, arguing that the party would have drawn a blank in the state without SP's support. Speaking to news agency PTI, Patel said the SP leadership had to persuade Gandhi to contest from Raebareli after he appeared unwilling to fight from Amethi, the traditional Gandhi family constituency. title: Travel firm demands additional Rs 2.98 lakh to change flight dates; commission orders Rs 5.43 lakh payout
text: AI generated image used for representative purpose NEW DELHI: A Delhi district consumer commission has directed a travel company to refund Rs 5.43 lakh to a family that was allegedly charged Rs 2.98 lakh to reschedule international flight tickets despite being told the tickets could be changed without additional charges. The commission also awarded Rs 30,000 as compensation and Rs 20,000 towards litigation expenses. The order was passed on September 18, 2026. Why did the family approach the consumer commission? According to the commission order, the complainants booked four open air tickets on April 6, 2024, for a total of Rs 5,43,551. The round-trip journey from Delhi to Amsterdam via Helsinki was scheduled for April 20, with the return journey on April 27 on Finnair Airlines. Before booking, the travel company allegedly assured the complainants that under its open ticket policy, the travel dates could be rescheduled within one year of booking without any additional fees, penalty or charges from the airline. On April 18, the complainants informed the travel company on WhatsApp group that their visas would not be processed in time and requested them to change the travel dates. The complainants received their visas on April 27. The travel company then asked for additional Rs 2.98 lakh on May 14 for changing the travel dates, following which the complainants sought refund of the entire ticket amount. The company, however, denied that it had promised free rescheduling. It alleged that it had merely acted as a travel agent facilitating the flight bookings and that rescheduling was something which falls under airline's jurisdiction. It also argued that the complainants had been informed that changes in travel dates would involve fare differences along with possible penalties. The travel company then claimed that the tickets were non-refundable and that any flexibility in rescheduling was subject to the airline's policies and applicable fare differences. The company also claimed that the complainants had delayed obtaining their visas and that their demand to waive the rescheduling charges was not justified. Why did the commission order a refund? The bench of president Monika Aggarwal Srivastava and members Dr Rajender Dhar and Ritu Garodia examined the documents submitted by both sides, including the WhatsApp chats produced by the complainants. It found that the family had been misled into believing that the tickets were open tickets. The commission said the demand for Rs 2.98 lakh to change the travel dates was unwarranted and unjustified. It observed that the travel company had indulged in mis-selling with the intention of extracting more money from the customers. The commission held that such conduct amounted to an unfair trade practice and concealment of hidden charges, besides being a deficiency in service. "OP has indulged in mis-selling with the intention of extracting more money from the customers. Such conduct amounts to unfair trade practice and concealment of hidden charges and, as such, constitutes deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on the part of OP," the commission said. The commission further noted that the complainants had paid Rs 5,43,551 for the tickets. Since they were faced with the additional Rs 2.98 lakh demand for rescheduling, they decided not to undertake the journey and sought a refund of the entire amount. "OP is directed to refund an amount of Rs.5,43,551/- along with interest of 6 percent per annum from the date of filing of the complaint, i.e. 19.09.2024, till its realisation. In case of failure to comply with the aforesaid direction, the entire amount shall carry interest of 7 percent per annum from the date of default till its realisation," the commission concluded. The commission held that the evidence, particularly the WhatsApp communication, supported the complainants' claim that they had been led to believe the tickets were open tickets. It therefore directed the company to refund the full ticket amount. What did the consumer commission order? The South II district consumer commission directed the travel company to: Refund Rs 5,43,551 to the complainants with 6 percent annual interest from September 19, 2024, until realisation. Pay Rs 30,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment. Pay Rs 20,000 towards litigation expenses. If the refund order is not complied with, the entire amount will carry 7 percent annual interest from the date of default until realisation. Comply with the order within 60 days from the date of its pronouncement.

title: Shohei Ohtaniâs 2023 donation of 60,000 baseball gloves to nearly 20,000 Japanese schools aimed to inspire future
text: Shohei Ohtaniâs 2023 donation of 60,000 baseball gloves to nearly 20,000 Japanese schools aimed to inspire futureÂ Shohei Ohtaniâs 60,000-glove donation to Japanese schools has given his off-field work a lasting place in Japanâs baseball story. The Los Angeles Dodgers star announced in November 2023 that about 60,000 youth gloves would be sent to roughly 20,000 elementary schools across Japan. Each school was set to receive three New Balance gloves, with two for right-handed players and one for left-handed players. The deliveries began in December 2023 and continued into March 2024. Ohtani said he hoped the gloves would give more children a chance to enjoy baseball and perhaps inspire future players to take up the sport. What did Shohei Ohtani donate to Japanâs elementary schools The idea was simple: put baseball gloves in schools so children could pick them up and play. Ohtani announced that every elementary school in Japan would receive three junior gloves, bringing the total to about 60,000 across roughly 20,000 schools. The New Balance gloves were made for younger children and came in three-per-school sets. Two were for right-handed throwers and one was for left-handed throwers. That detail mattered because it meant left-handed students were included from the start rather than being left without suitable equipment. The programme also covered more than ordinary public elementary schools. New Balance said the distribution included national, public and private elementary schools, compulsory education schools and special-needs schools. The company handled deliveries through education boards and schools, allowing the gloves to reach children across Japan. Ohtani also wanted the gift to carry a personal message. The boxes included his signature and the words âLetâs play baseball!â in Japanese. His message was aimed at children who might not otherwise get the chance to try the sport. Ohtani explained why he wanted to do it: âIâm hoping the kids can spend their days happily with a lot of energy through baseball,â Ohtani wrote. âIâll be looking forward to sharing the field one day with someone that grew up using this glove!â Why did Shohei Ohtani want children to play baseball Ohtaniâs own childhood was an important part of the idea. He grew up playing baseball in Japan before moving to Nippon Professional Baseball and later Major League Baseball. By sending equipment directly to schools, he created an easy way for children to have their first experience with the sport. The official New Balance announcement said Ohtani wanted children to experience the fun of baseball and hoped the programme would help spread the sport while supporting childrenâs physical activity and health. The school setting also made the plan different from a donation aimed only at organised baseball teams. Children did not need to belong to a club to come across the gloves. They could see and use them through school activities. That was especially important for beginners. A child does not need to understand every part of baseball to start throwing a ball. A few gloves in a school can make that first step much easier. The message from Ohtani also looked beyond the donation itself. He was not only giving away equipment. He was imagining a future in which children who started playing with those gloves could one day meet him on a baseball field. In his official statement, Ohtani said: âI would like to send my appreciation to everyone that was involved and helped this project come true.â How were Shohei Ohtani and New Balance involved New Balance played a direct role in the project. The company was Ohtaniâs footwear and apparel partner and supplied the junior gloves used for the school programme. The gloves were not simply regular products taken from store shelves. They were designed for younger players and prepared specifically for the donation. Each school received the same three-glove combination, with two right-handed gloves and one left-handed glove. The scale of the project was also unusual. About 60,000 gloves had to be distributed across approximately 20,000 schools. New Balance said the deliveries were scheduled from December 2023 through March 2024. The gloves also were not being introduced as a normal retail product. That kept the focus of the programme on giving schools equipment for children rather than turning the donated gloves into a regular product line. For Ohtani, the timing of the announcement also drew attention because he was one of baseballâs biggest free agents at the time. He later signed a 10-year, $700 million contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers. But the glove project itself was announced before that deal was completed. The donation therefore became one of the major off-field stories surrounding Ohtani during that period. It connected his growing international profile with the sport he first learned as a child in Japan. What happened after Shohei Ohtaniâs gloves reached schools The donation became more than a headline once the gloves began arriving at schools. In 2024, MLB reported on one Tokyo girlsâ elementary school that received the gloves and held an event for its students. The school had already been introducing children to baseball, and the new equipment gave them another way to try the sport. For some children, the gloves were their first chance to play baseball. One student at the school had previously been practising by throwing a ball against a wall and catching it. She said she wanted to play baseball but did not have the equipment to begin. The arrival of the glove changed that. She later began playing catch with her father. That example showed what Ohtaniâs wider plan was trying to achieve. The donation did not promise that every child would become a baseball player. Instead, it removed one simple barrier: not having a glove. With two right-handed gloves and one left-handed glove at each school, students with different throwing hands could be included. Ohtaniâs message has therefore travelled well beyond the original announcement. What began as a plan for about 60,000 gloves became a nationwide school programme involving roughly 20,000 elementary schools. For a player who built his career around both pitching and hitting, the project offered another way to influence baseball in Japan. This time, there was no stadium, scoreboard or professional contract involved. It was about putting a glove into a childâs hands and giving that child a chance to play. title: Nabha jailbreak: HC grants regular bail to key conspirator Romi
text: Patiala : In a reprieve for extradited gangster Ramanjit Singh alias Romi, the Punjab and Haryana high court has granted him regular bail in the 2016 Nabha high-security jailbreak case, which includes charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Setting aside a July 13 order by the Additional Sessions Judge, Patiala, a division bench comprising Justice Vinod S Bhardwaj and Justice Ravinder Malik ruled that Romi was entitled to bail after spending over eight years in continuous detention, while the trial against him remained at an infant stage. The relief follows an Aug 14 order by a Nabha magistrate granting Romi bail in an allied vehicle theft and forgery case, effectively securing him bail in both cases registered at Kotwali Nabha police station, said Romiâs counsel Shivam Sukheeja. Defence counsel Tanu Bedi, appearing alongside advocates Ankur Goyat and Ashish Pundir in the high court, submitted that Romi had been detained in Hong Kong since June 26, 2018, following an extradition request by India, before being brought to Amritsar Central Jail on Aug 23, 2024. Highlighting proportionality, the defence argued that similarly placed co-conspirators who stood trial had already received a maximum sentence of 10 years, meaning Romi had completed over 80% of his potential term. Furthermore, only one out of 151 prosecution witnesses had been partly examined so far. The senior deputy advocate general opposed the plea, arguing that Romi arranged foreign funding and logistical support for the escape. However, the bench held that prolonged custody, the slow pace of the trial and the 10-year benchmark awarded to co-accused warranted regular bail, subject to bail bonds and a strict bar against influencing witnesses. On Nov 27, 2016, around 15 to 20 armed assailants in police uniforms stormed the maximum security jail in Nabha, looted automatic rifles and fled in a four-vehicle convoy, freeing six high-profile prisoners. Based on disclosures by arrested gangsters Gurpreet Sekhon and Chanpreet Singh, investigators identified Romi as the Hong Kong-based mastermind behind arranging safe houses, vehicles and funding for the attackers. Romi was arrested via an Interpol Red Corner notice in Hong Kong in 2018 and extradited to India in Aug 2024 following protracted treaty litigation. In March 2023, Patiala Additional Sessions Judge H S Grewal convicted 22 accused in the primary jailbreak trial and acquitted six â Tejinder Sharma, Naresh Narang, Ravinder Vicky, Ranjit Singh, Mohammad Aasim and Jatinder â for lack of evidence. Eighteen convicts received 10-year rigorous imprisonment terms, including compromised officials assistant jail superintendent Bheem Singh and head warder Jagmeet Singh, who facilitated arms smuggling into the barracks. Bikkar Singh and Sukhchain Singh received 20 years on concurrent NDPS charges, while Gurpreet Mangewal and Sunil Kalra received five and three years, respectively. Ground assault commander Palwinder Singh alias Pinda was intercepted in Shamli, Uttar Pradesh, shortly after the escape. The Six Escapees Harminder Singh Mintoo (KLF Chief): Arrested within 24 hours in New Delhi; died of cardiac arrest in jail in April 2018 Harjinder Singh alias Vicky Gounder: Killed alongside associate Prema Lahoriya in a Jan 2018 police encounter Gurpreet Singh Sekhon, Kulpreet Singh alias Neeta Deol, and Amandeep Singh Dhotian: Recaptured between 2016 and 2017; each was awarded 10-year sentences in 2023. However, Sekhon got bail in November that year following suspension of sentence by the high court.
